title: Quantum Signal Processing Phase Factorization Via Logarithmic Derivatives
authors: Christopher Peng
abstract: ArXiv:2610.14259v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum signal processing (QSP) requires the efficient computation of phase factors associated with a polynomial transformation. One existing stable factorization method avoids direct root finding but relies on Prony's method to recover a polynomial from weighted power sums of its roots (arXiv:2202.02671). We present a modification of this approach that eliminates Prony's method by using the logarithmic derivative of an associated polynomial. Because the logarithmic derivative has the same residue at every root after accounting for multiplicity, its Fourier coefficients directly yield the unweighted power sums of the roots inside the unit disk. The Newton--Girard identities then recover the coefficients of the corresponding polynomial without computing its roots. The resulting algorithm has [MATH] computational complexity and simplifies the factorization procedure of the original method. In numerical experiments on Hamiltonian simulation, eigenstate filtering, matrix inversion, and the Fermi--Dirac operator, our implementation computes phase factors in seconds with maximum errors on the order of [MATH].
tldr: A modified stable factorization algorithm for quantum signal processing phase factors that uses logarithmic derivatives to avoid Prony's method.
motivation: Quantum signal processing requires efficient and stable computation of phase factors for polynomial transformations, and existing root-finding or Prony-based methods can be cumbersome or unstable.
method: The paper replaces Prony's method with the logarithmic derivative of an associated polynomial; because the logarithmic derivative has equal residues at all roots, its Fourier coefficients directly yield unweighted power sums, which are then used with Newton-Girard identities to recover polynomial coefficients without root finding.
result: The algorithm achieves computational complexity [MATH] and numerical experiments on Hamiltonian simulation, eigenstate filtering, matrix inversion, and the Fermi-Dirac operator show phase factors computed in seconds with maximum errors on the order of [MATH].
conclusion: The proposed method simplifies and stabilizes QSP phase-factor computation, offering a practical alternative for polynomial transformations in quantum algorithms.

title: Competitive Scaling Of Small-subsystem-optimization Heuristics For Labs
authors: Adil A. Gangat Ginger E. Lau
abstract: ArXiv:2610.14361v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The low autocorrelation binary sequences (LABS) problem, often formulated as a spin-lattice energy-minimization problem, is a combinatorial optimization problem with a very rugged energy landscape. We demonstrate that iterative optimization of very small subsystems of n spins that are decoupled from the rest of the system achieves global optimization of LABS with a time-to-solution scaling that is competitive with heuristics that optimize the global system of N spins directly. Our isolated-subsystem heuristic with n = 4 achieves a time scaling of O(1.333N ) on the interval N = [27, 60], while the current state-of-the-art classical and quantum scalings are respectively O(1.34N ) and O(1.21N ). Our results suggest that specialized optimization hardware with only small numbers of logical spins may be of practical relevance.
tldr: The paper studies small-subsystem-optimization heuristics for the low autocorrelation binary sequences problem and finds scaling competitive with global optimization heuristics.
motivation: The LABS problem is a rugged combinatorial optimization task, and the authors ask whether optimizing only very small subsystems can achieve global optimization with competitive time scaling.
method: They iteratively optimize small decoupled subsystems of n spins and benchmark the time-to-solution scaling against state-of-the-art classical and quantum heuristics for LABS.
result: Their n = 4 isolated-subsystem heuristic achieves O(1.333^N) scaling on N = [27, 60], competitive with classical O(1.34^N) and quantum O(1.21^N) scalings.
conclusion: The results suggest that specialized optimization hardware with only a small number of logical spins may be practically relevant for LABS-like problems.

title: Quadrature-detected Zero-to-ultralow-field Nuclear Magnetic Resonance
authors: Anne M. Fabricant, Florin Teleanu, Adam Ortmeier, Piotr Put, Seth Dilday, Alexej Jerschow, Dmitry Budker, Thomas Theis, Danila A. Barskiy
abstract: ArXiv:2610.14451v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present the concept of quadrature-detected zero-to-ultralow-field nuclear magnetic resonance (QD ZULF NMR). Two orthogonal sensors, atomic optically pumped magnetometers, are used to separately detect components of oscillating sample magnetization, which are then combined into a quadrature signal. This approach enables the distinction of positive and negative resonance frequencies with respect to the laboratory frame---such that absolute signs of gyromagnetic ratios can be determined. In addition, QD ZULF NMR reduces peak density and overlap compared to ZULF NMR with single-axis detection, while providing richer information about nuclear-spin dynamics. As an illustration, we present experimental [MATH]-spectra for thermally polarized [[MATH]C]-formic acid and [[MATH]C]-methanol, compounds commonly used in ZULF NMR which represent XA and XA[MATH] spin systems, respectively. A theoretical framework describing QD ZULF NMR signals is provided.
tldr: The paper introduces quadrature-detected zero-to-ultralow-field NMR using two orthogonal atomic magnetometers to distinguish positive and negative resonance frequencies and reduce spectral overlap.
motivation: Conventional ZULF NMR with single-axis detection cannot distinguish the signs of resonance frequencies and suffers from peak overlap, limiting the extraction of complete nuclear-spin information.
method: Two orthogonal optically pumped magnetometers separately detect oscillating sample magnetization components, which are combined into a quadrature signal; a theoretical framework for QD ZULF NMR signals is provided.
result: Experimental 13C spectra for thermally polarized formic acid and methanol demonstrate reduced peak density and overlap, enabling determination of absolute gyromagnetic ratio signs and providing richer nuclear-spin dynamics.
conclusion: QD ZULF NMR enhances spectral resolution and information content for ZULF NMR, with potential applications in chemical analysis and spin-dynamics studies, though it lies outside the core quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, and hybrid quantum systems directions.

title: Memory-Augmented Phase-Field Modeling: Onsager Formulation, Internal-Variable Lifting, And Structure-Preserving Computation
authors: Peng Ding, Qingxia Liu, Zhiping Mao, Zhen Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2610.14466v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, we develop a general memory-augmented phase-field (MAPF) framework based on Onsager's variational principle, in which memory effects are incorporated through a general relaxation kernel while preserving the thermodynamic consistency of the underlying system. Rather than treating fractional models as fundamental formulations, we show that they can be interpreted as reduced descriptions associated with specific power-law memory kernels. The proposed MAPF equations provide a unified modeling framework for non-Markovian phase-field dynamics. To facilitate analysis and computation, we further introduce an equivalent internal-variable representation that transforms the original nonlocal-in-time dynamics into an extended Markovian gradient system. This formulation preserves key structural properties, including energy dissipation and mass conservation, and enables the development of efficient structure-preserving numerical schemes. In particular, we construct an energy-stable scalar auxiliary variable approach combined with a fast rank-one implementation that exploits the relaxation-spectrum-induced coupling structure, resulting in a computationally efficient algorithm with reduced storage requirements. The proposed framework establishes a systematic connection between memory-dependent phase-field modeling, internal-variable thermodynamics, and structure-preserving numerical computation. Numerical experiments demonstrate the accuracy, stability, and efficiency of the proposed methods for phase-field dynamics with long-time memory effects.
tldr: A memory-augmented phase-field framework based on Onsager's variational principle that unifies non-Markovian dynamics via internal-variable lifting and structure-preserving computation.
motivation: Phase-field models often neglect memory effects, and fractional models are used ad hoc without a clear thermodynamic foundation.
method: The authors incorporate memory via a general relaxation kernel, reinterpret fractional models as power-law kernels, and transform the nonlocal-in-time dynamics into an extended Markovian gradient system using internal variables.
result: The equivalent internal-variable formulation preserves energy dissipation and mass conservation, enabling energy-stable scalar auxiliary variable schemes with fast rank-one implementation and reduced storage.
conclusion: The MAPF framework systematically connects memory-dependent phase-field modeling, internal-variable thermodynamics, and structure-preserving numerical computation, as demonstrated by numerical experiments.

title: Intrinsic Contraction Theory And Stabilization Of Probability Measures On The Wasserstein Space
authors: Min Kim, Joshua D. Ibrahim, Soon-Jo Chung
abstract: ArXiv:2610.14164v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Deterministic flows can contract Wasserstein distances between probability laws without being contractive in point-state space. We develop a differential contraction theory for pushforward flows on forward-invariant subsets of the 2-Wasserstein space that quotients out the gauge freedom of the continuity equation. Weighted Helmholtz-Hodge decomposition and the Wasserstein contingent cone define the weighted horizontal tangent cone (whtc). Requiring the contraction quadratic form to be nonpositive only on the whtc yields the Intrinsic Wasserstein Contraction Condition (IWCC), which generalizes the classical contraction LMI and recovers it on Dirac measures. An almost-everywhere Euler approximation based on the superposition principle and Banach-valued Lebesgue differentiation theorem proves that IWCC is sufficient for intrinsic Wasserstein contraction. Law contraction without point-state contraction is illustrated by a rotationally symmetric shear example. Finally, a new comparison lemma yields an incremental Wasserstein ISS theorem; for Brockett's integrator, we prove exponential stabilization of a class of axisymmetric laws to the uniform law on a circle via a smooth feedback.
tldr: The paper develops a differential contraction theory for probability measure flows on the Wasserstein space and proves stabilization results for certain probability laws.
motivation: Deterministic flows can contract Wasserstein distances between probability laws even when they are not contractive in point-state space, motivating a theory of intrinsic contraction on the Wasserstein space.
method: The authors use weighted Helmholtz-Hodge decomposition and the Wasserstein contingent cone to define a weighted horizontal tangent cone, introduce the Intrinsic Wasserstein Contraction Condition, and prove sufficiency via an almost-everywhere Euler approximation.
result: The framework generalizes the classical contraction LMI to measure-valued flows and yields an incremental Wasserstein ISS theorem, with an application to exponential stabilization of axisymmetric laws for Brockett's integrator.
conclusion: The work provides a rigorous control-theoretic foundation for contraction and stabilization of probability measures on the Wasserstein space, extending classical contraction analysis beyond point-state systems.

title: Limitations On Autoregressive Token Generation Via Sequential Sampling
authors: Gal Arnon, Andrej Bogdanov, Paul Lou, Giulio Malavolta, Alon Rosen, Lorenzo Taschin
abstract: ArXiv:2610.14615v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study autoregressive token generation through the notion of sequential samplers: A circuit that samples the next symbol only given the previous ones and possibly a small amount of state. We show that (1) a sequential sampler with [MATH] bits of state can be simulated by a stateless one at a roughly [MATH] size overhead; (2) efficient insertional sampling (Stern, Chan, Kiros, Uszkoreit, ICML 2019) is more powerful than efficient sequential sampling in any fixed order; (3) sequential samplers with small state cannot establish certain forms of covert cryptographic channels. Result (1), together with the pseudoentropy vs. sequential sampleability duality of Vadhan and Zheng (STOC 2012), characterizes efficient sequential sampleability with small state. Result (3) provides a potential safety mechanism against subliminal coordination among malicious LLM agents.
tldr: The paper studies autoregressive token generation via sequential samplers and shows limitations on state, order, and covert cryptographic channel establishment.
motivation: Autoregressive models such as LLMs generate tokens sequentially, raising questions about the computational resources needed and whether such samplers can support covert communication.
method: The authors formalize sequential samplers as circuits with limited state and prove simulation overheads, power separations against insertional sampling, and constraints on covert channels.
result: They show that small-state sequential samplers can be simulated statelessly with roughly exponential overhead, insertional sampling is strictly more powerful, and small-state samplers cannot establish certain covert cryptographic channels.
conclusion: These results characterize efficient sequential sampleability with small state and suggest a safety mechanism against subliminal coordination among malicious LLM agents.

title: Bipartite Carrier Compression And Machine-Certified Bounds In Sch\"onhage Trilinear Multiplication Tensors
authors: Volkan Da\u{g}l{\i}, Zerrin Da\u{g}l{\i}, Da\u{g}han Da\u{g}l{\i}
abstract: ArXiv:2610.14263v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Under the conditional framework breaking the longstanding O(n log n) integer multiplication barrier (originating from OpenAI Preprint #109), the asymptotic time complexity exponent T(n) = O(n (log n)^{1-\kappa}) is governed by bounding the second moment E[X^2] < 1 of recursive branching processes over trilinear tensor carrier graphs. In this work, we present a constructive combinatorial optimization over the alternating carrier bipartite matching graphs of the Sch\"onhage trilinear tensor decomposition at dimensions h=23 and h=25. Through an alternating augmenting path search, we uncover a non-trivial cluster-unlocking cascade that eliminates 185 carrier roles (95 roles in h=23 and 90 roles in h=25), reducing the global physical wire width by 377,890 wires from the reviewed baseline W = 177,284,805 down to W = 176,906,915. Evaluated over the exact 10^{-14} rational grid, this wire reduction certifies an improved second-moment coefficient AB = 5,164,059 / 125,000,000,000 and establishes the sharpened conditional exponent \kappa = 826,215,307 / 20,000,000,000,000 \approx 4.131076535 \times 10^{-5}, strictly surpassing the preceding record on this architecture (\kappa \approx 4.123864 \times 10^{-5}). All 47 polynomial constraints and 7 rational security margins are audited in exact Q-arithmetic with zero floating-point error, and the fundamental wire reduction identity is formally verified in the Lean 4 interactive theorem prover without unproven axioms.
tldr: This paper performs a combinatorial optimization on Schonhage trilinear multiplication tensors to reduce carrier roles and wires, enabling a slightly improved conditional exponent for integer multiplication, with Lean-verified bounds.
motivation: The work aims to advance the conditional framework for breaking the O(n log n) integer multiplication barrier by sharpening the exponent through exact rational arithmetic and formal verification.
method: It constructs alternating carrier bipartite matching graphs for Schonhage trilinear tensor decompositions at dimensions h=23 and h=25, uses augmenting path search to remove carrier roles, and audits constraints in exact Q-arithmetic and Lean 4.
result: The optimization eliminates 185 carrier roles, reduces wire width by 377,890 wires, certifies a new second-moment coefficient, and yields a sharpened conditional exponent kappa ≈ 4.131076535 × 10^-5, improving the previous record.
conclusion: The paper demonstrates a machine-certified improvement in the Schonhage multiplication tensor framework, though it is highly specialized to classical computational complexity and formal verification without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: How Long Is A Photon?
authors: Sky Nelson-Isaacs
abstract: ArXiv:2610.14088v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A photon has the strange property that it travels along a null interval with zero proper time, hence its emission and absorption points are, in a sense, a singular event. For their part, the emission and absorption processes have a finite duration which determines the spectral content of the photon. The question in the title points to the conceptual difficulty in `stitching' together these three intervals, which all correspond to the same physical entity but have fundamentally incompatible temporal descriptions. A previously developed model for quantum wavefunction propagation solves this apparent dilemma by formulating the life cycle of a photon in terms of recursive Fourier transforms on dual spaces. Because it doesn't treat space as dependent on time, and it is built on the Fourier transform whose phase is an invariant in special relativity as well as the foundation of the uncertainty principle, the model is a promising candidate framework for making quantum mechanics compatible with relativity. The model proposes to serve as an improved Klein-Gordon equation, or relativistically compatible replacement for Schr\"{o}dinger's equation.
tldr: Proposes a recursive Fourier transform model on dual spaces to reconcile a photon's null-interval propagation with the finite duration of its emission and absorption.
motivation: The photon has zero proper time between emission and absorption, yet those processes have finite durations, creating incompatible temporal descriptions that challenge quantum-relativistic consistency.
method: Formulates the photon life cycle using recursive Fourier transforms on dual spaces, avoiding treating space as dependent on time and leveraging the relativistic invariance of the Fourier phase.
result: Claims the model resolves the temporal stitching dilemma and can serve as a relativistically compatible replacement for the Schrödinger equation or an improved Klein-Gordon equation.
conclusion: The work is a foundational quantum-relativity proposal that is not directly connected to quantum information, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Spatial Nonlocality From Finite Extinction Ratio In Botdr Over Heterogeneous Fiber Links
authors: Giannis Poulopoulos, Constantinos Haliotis, Panagiotis Toumasis, Hercules Avramopoulos
abstract: ArXiv:2610.14128v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Finite extinction ratio in pulse-modulated Brillouin optical time-domain reflectometry (BOTDR) produces residual inter-pulse Brillouin backscatter outside the nominal pulse gate. We model and experimentally quantify this effect as spatial nonlocality in a heterogeneous fiber link and define the spectral contamination ratio (SCR) as the contaminating Brillouin-band power normalized to the local Brillouin-band power. Measurements were performed using a 1.2 km standard single-mode fiber (SMF) followed by 0.1 km of dispersion-compensating fiber (DCF), whose separated Brillouin frequency shifts allow section-to-section leakage to be resolved spectrally. At 20 m spatial resolution, increasing the extinction ratio from 18.5 to 33.0 dB reduced the SMF-band contamination in the DCF gates from -5.3 to -14.8 dB. Over the 16-33 dB range, the SCR showed fitted slopes of -1.064 and -1.246 dB/dB for the two contamination directions. These results quantify finite-ER-induced spatial nonlocality and provide a link-specific metric for extinction-ratio selection in BOTDR.
tldr: Finite extinction ratio in BOTDR causes residual inter-pulse Brillouin backscatter, quantified as spectral contamination ratio (SCR) in a heterogeneous fiber link.
motivation: Pulse-modulated Brillouin optical time-domain reflectometry (BOTDR) suffers from finite extinction ratio, leading to leakage outside the nominal pulse gate that degrades spatial resolution and measurement accuracy.
method: The authors model and experimentally measure spatial nonlocality using a 1.2 km standard single-mode fiber followed by 0.1 km dispersion-compensating fiber, resolving section-to-section leakage spectrally via separated Brillouin frequency shifts while varying extinction ratio from 18.5 to 33.0 dB.
result: Increasing extinction ratio from 18.5 to 33.0 dB reduced SMF-band contamination in DCF gates from -5.3 to -14.8 dB, with fitted SCR slopes of -1.064 and -1.246 dB/dB for the two contamination directions.
conclusion: The work quantifies finite-extinction-ratio-induced spatial nonlocality and provides a link-specific metric for extinction-ratio selection in BOTDR.

title: An Introduction To The $p$-Differential Forms In Spinor Variables On The Minkowskian Manifold
authors: Julio C\'esar Jaramillo Quiceno
abstract: ArXiv:2610.14240v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This article presents an introductory study of [MATH]-differential forms in spinor variables defined on the Minkowskian (or Lorentzian) manifold. Starting from the algebraic and geometric foundations of spinor spaces and Clifford algebras, we establish the correspondence between Minkowski spacetime and Hermitian matrices in spinor coordinates. Within this framework, we construct differential 1-forms and 2-forms expressed in spinor notation, and formulate the Dirac operator in terms of exterior calculus. Furthermore, we extend this approach to the case of non-monogenic functions, following the method proposed in~. The results illustrate the consistency of the spinorial exterior calculus and its potential applications in the study of relativistic field equations and geometric formulations of quantum theory.
tldr: Introduces p-differential forms in spinor variables on the Minkowskian manifold, constructing an exterior calculus and Dirac operator in spinor notation.
motivation: To develop a spinorial exterior calculus for relativistic field equations and geometric formulations of quantum theory.
method: Starting from spinor spaces and Clifford algebras, the work maps Minkowski spacetime to Hermitian matrices in spinor coordinates, constructs differential 1-forms and 2-forms, and formulates the Dirac operator via exterior calculus, extending to non-monogenic functions.
result: The paper establishes the consistency of the spinorial exterior calculus and indicates potential applications in relativistic field equations and geometric quantum theory.
conclusion: It provides an introductory framework for spinorial differential forms on Minkowskian manifolds, with possible use in relativistic and geometric formulations, but lacks direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: Interpretation Of Chirality Imprinted On Photoelectron Momentum Spectra By Three-dimensional Light Fields
authors: Junxin Yuan, Yuhong Li, Fei Li, Jinkai Zhang, Shiyang Zhong, Hao Teng, Yujun Yang, Yingchun Guo, Zhiyi Wei, Jing Chen, Xiaojun Liu, Bingbing Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2610.14557v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Synthetic three-dimensional (3D) light fields provide a new route to imprinting chirality on achiral matter through light--matter interaction. Although previous work has numerically demonstrated that chirality can be imprinted on the photoelectron momentum spectrum of atoms, a transparent analytical physical picture that links the structure of the driving field to the chirality of the spectrum is still an open question. Here, using frequency-domain theory based on nonperturbative quantum electrodynamics (QED), we demonstrate that this chirality originates from coherence between adjacent quantum transition channels. We further find that a symmetry transformation introduces into the coherence term a symmetry-breaking phase shift ([MATH]), which can be tuned by varying the laser-field parameters to preserve or break the corresponding symmetry in the spectrum. Once all such symmetries are broken, the momentum spectrum becomes chiral. In particular, for the noncollinear two-color 3D light field considered here, the spectrum is chiral for even [MATH] and achiral for odd [MATH]. Our results provide a microscopic interpretation of chirality imprinting and establish a framework for predicting and controlling chiral electron wave packets with synthetic 3D light fields.
tldr: An analytical frequency-domain QED study explains how chirality is imprinted on photoelectron momentum spectra by synthetic 3D light fields, tracing it to coherence between adjacent quantum transition channels.
motivation: Synthetic 3D light fields can imprint chirality on achiral matter, but a transparent analytical picture linking the driving-field structure to the chirality of the photoelectron spectrum was missing.
method: The authors use frequency-domain theory based on nonperturbative quantum electrodynamics to analyze the photoelectron momentum spectrum generated by a noncollinear two-color 3D light field, identifying symmetry-breaking phase shifts in the coherence terms.
result: Chirality originates from coherence between adjacent quantum transition channels, and a tunable symmetry-breaking phase shift controls whether the spectrum is chiral; for the considered field, the spectrum is chiral for even values and achiral for odd values.
conclusion: The work provides a microscopic interpretation of chirality imprinting and establishes a framework for predicting and controlling chiral electron wave packets with synthetic 3D light fields.

title: Maximal Axion Optical Chirality Enabled By Degenerate Quasibound States In The Continuum
authors: Chang-Yin Ji, Chong Wang, Jiafang Li, Yugui Yao
abstract: ArXiv:2610.14611v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Axion quasiparticles introduce magnetoelectric coupling in topological materials, yet their optical signatures are intrinsically weak, severely limiting experimental detection and practical exploitation. Here, we demonstrate maximal optical chirality of axion quasiparticles by coupling them with degenerate quasibound states in the continuum (qBICs). By integrating three-dimensional topological insulators (3DTIs) with achiral photonic crystal slabs (PCSs), we reveal that axion quasiparticles induce an effective Zeeman effect that lifts the degeneracy of achiral qBICs in PCSs, splitting them into two nondegenerate high-Q chiral qBICs with maximally opposite chirality. These result in a more than 10^3- and 200-fold increase in the polarization conversion efficiency and Faraday rotation angle, respectively, compared to the intrinsic chiroptical response of bare 3DTI films. Moreover, circular dichroism and nonreciprocal optical responses are revealed as new key signatures for probing axion quasiparticles in 3DTI-PCS coupled systems. Our results provide a definitive route for observing axion quasiparticles and topological physics, while establishing a promising platform for controlling optical polarization, spin, phase, and nonreciprocal responses.
tldr: Coupling axion quasiparticles in 3D topological insulators to degenerate quasibound states in the continuum yields maximally chiral, high-Q optical resonances with greatly enhanced nonreciprocal and chiroptical responses.
motivation: Axion quasiparticles in topological materials produce magnetoelectric coupling, but their optical signatures are extremely weak, hindering experimental detection and practical use.
method: The authors integrate three-dimensional topological insulators with achiral photonic crystal slabs supporting degenerate quasibound states in the continuum, which the axion-induced effective Zeeman effect splits into two nondegenerate high-Q chiral qBICs.
result: Polarization conversion efficiency and Faraday rotation angle are enhanced by more than 10^3-fold and 200-fold respectively, with circular dichroism and nonreciprocal responses emerging as new signatures of axion quasiparticles.
conclusion: The 3DTI-PCS platform offers a route to observe axion quasiparticles and topological physics while providing a means to control optical polarization, spin, phase, and nonreciprocity.

title: Near-focus Intensity Evolution Of Spatiotemporal Optical Vortex Pulses And Consequences For Their Nonlinear Upconversion
authors: Titouan Gadeyne, Vartika Vishnoi, Thierry Ruchon
abstract: ArXiv:2610.14640v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Spatiotemporal optical vortex (STOV) laser pulses are attracting attention for their puzzling transverse orbital angular momentum (OAM) and propagation properties, which could determine their future applications. While the characteristic reshaping of their space-time envelope upon diffraction from the focal plane to the far-field is now well-established, the evolution of their intensity as they propagate has not been studied quantitatively, despite growing interest for their use in nonlinear optics and strong-field physics. Here, we explore experimentally and analytically the focusing dynamics of STOVs produced by a pulse shaper, and evidence a substantial longitudinal shift between the coordinate at which a circularly-symmetric STOV forms and that at which the pulse reaches its peak intensity. To illustrate some practical consequences for applications, we experimentally demonstrate how the yield of second-harmonic generation can consequently be maximized several Rayleigh lengths beyond the plane where the circular STOV really occurs. These results signal careful characterization of spatiotemporal pulses as a requisite for nonlinear optical experiments, and pave the way for finer control of complex laser drivers for light-matter interactions.
tldr: The paper characterizes the focusing dynamics of spatiotemporal optical vortex (STOV) pulses, revealing a longitudinal offset between the circular-STOV formation plane and the peak-intensity plane, and exploits this to optimize second-harmonic generation.
motivation: STOV pulses exhibit unusual transverse orbital angular momentum and reshaping upon propagation, but their longitudinal intensity evolution had not been quantified despite growing interest in nonlinear-optics and strong-field applications.
method: The authors combine pulse-shaper generation of STOVs with experimental and analytical studies of focusing dynamics, and measure second-harmonic generation yield as a function of propagation distance.
result: A substantial longitudinal shift is found between the plane where a circularly symmetric STOV forms and the plane of peak intensity, and SHG can be maximized several Rayleigh lengths beyond the STOV formation plane.
conclusion: Careful characterization of spatiotemporal pulse structure is essential for nonlinear optical experiments and enables finer control of complex laser drivers for light-matter interactions.

title: Reducing Trust Cost In Quantum Application Development Using Ai
authors: Katsuhiro Endo
abstract: ArXiv:2610.14665v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Generative AI can be a powerful tool for supporting the design and implementation of quantum applications, whereas the burden of checking whether generated circuits realize the intended computation increases. In this study, we regard this burden of human understanding, checking, and judgment as ``trust cost,'' and propose a development methodology that integrates AI and formal verification to reduce it. In the proposed development methodology, the implementation is divided into three components: a target mathematical specification, a quantum circuit, and a correspondence theorem and its proof that prove the agreement between the two. This division separates the specifications and theorem statements checked by humans from the theorem proofs entrusted to mechanical checking. As a concrete development example of this proposal, we describe an implementation for the time evolution of a stochastic particle system and its results.
tldr: The paper proposes an AI-assisted development methodology that integrates formal verification to reduce the human trust cost when building quantum applications.
motivation: Generative AI can help design and implement quantum applications, but it increases the burden of checking whether generated circuits match the intended computation.
method: The implementation is divided into a target mathematical specification, a quantum circuit, and a correspondence theorem with proof; humans check specifications and theorem statements while mechanical tools check proofs.
result: The authors present a concrete development example for the time evolution of a stochastic particle system and report initial results.
conclusion: The proposed methodology aims to lower trust cost in quantum application development by separating human understanding from mechanical verification.

title: Quantitative Stability And Sample Complexity For Regularized Gromov-Wasserstein Distance
authors: Xiaohui Chen Pengtao Li
abstract: ArXiv:2610.14562v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Gromov-Wasserstein (GW) distance provides a principled framework for comparing two probability distributions supported on different metric spaces by matching their individual intrinsic geometric structures. In practice, the GW distance is estimated from finite samples and often incorporates regularization for statistical and computational tractability. This motivates a quantitative understanding of the stability and estimation error of regularized GW distances. In this work, we study a general family of divergence regularized GW distances, including entropy and Tsallis regularizations over the full range of powers, from a nonasymptotic perspective. Specifically, we establish Lipschitz continuity of the value of regularized GW and H{\"o}lder continuity of its optimal coupling under Wasserstein perturbations of the input probability measures. Moreover, we derive the parametric rate of convergence for the empirical regularized (2,2)-GW distance on compactly supported Euclidean spaces.
tldr: The paper establishes nonasymptotic stability bounds and parametric convergence rates for regularized Gromov-Wasserstein distances estimated from finite samples.
motivation: Gromov-Wasserstein distances are widely used to compare distributions on different metric spaces, but in practice they are computed from finite samples with regularization, motivating a quantitative understanding of their stability and estimation error.
method: The authors analyze a general family of divergence-regularized GW distances (including entropy and Tsallis regularizations across all powers), proving Lipschitz continuity of the value and Hölder continuity of the optimal coupling under Wasserstein perturbations, and deriving the parametric convergence rate for empirical regularized (2,2)-GW on compactly supported Euclidean spaces.
result: They obtain quantitative stability guarantees under input measure perturbations and show the empirical regularized (2,2)-GW distance converges at the parametric rate.
conclusion: The results provide a rigorous statistical foundation for using regularized Gromov-Wasserstein distances in practice, characterizing their robustness and sample complexity.

title: Products Of Berezin Transforms On Generalized Fock Spaces
authors: Hao Tian
abstract: ArXiv:2610.14599v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study products [MATH] of Berezin transforms on generalized Fock spaces over [MATH]. We establish a result for [MATH]: if [MATH] coincides with another such product, then the weight parameters of the second product must be [MATH]. As consequences, we characterize when two Berezin transforms commute and when the product of two Berezin transforms is again a Berezin transform.
tldr: The paper studies products of Berezin transforms on generalized Fock spaces over C^n, characterizing when such products coincide, commute, or reduce to a single Berezin transform.
motivation: Berezin transforms are fundamental objects in complex analysis and operator theory on Fock spaces, but their algebraic properties under composition and products on generalized Fock spaces are not fully understood.
method: The author analyzes products of Berezin transforms on generalized Fock spaces over C^n and derives conditions on weight parameters for two such products to be equal.
result: If a product of Berezin transforms coincides with another such product, then the weight parameters of the second product must match; as consequences, commutation and product-closure conditions are characterized.
conclusion: The work provides a mathematical characterization of products and commutativity of Berezin transforms on generalized Fock spaces, contributing to complex analysis rather than quantum information theory.

title: Memory-Coupled Unlearning For Data-Absent Identity Forgetting
authors: Chun-I Fan, Lu-En Chen, Ming-Feng Tsai, Tomohiro Morikawa
abstract: ArXiv:2610.14148v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Machine unlearning aims to reduce the influence of designated training data from a trained model while preserving its utility on retained data. Identity-level unlearning is particularly challenging when only limited target-specific information is available when a forgetting request is processed. In this work, we propose Memory-Coupled Unlearning (MCU), a framework that augments a host model with a Modern Hopfield Network (MHN) serving as a controllable external identity-prototype memory. During prototype construction, feature representations associated with each training identity are aggregated into identity prototypes and stored in the MHN. A Prototype Adaptation Network (PAN) transforms the retrieved memory representation, while a Dependency Gating Unit (DGU) controls its contribution to downstream prediction. When an identity is requested to be forgotten, MCU first removes the corresponding prototype from the external memory and subsequently readapts the model using limited support information associated with the target identities together with retained data. Importantly, in this work, ``data-absent'' specifically refers to the absence of the complete original forget set during request-time gradient-based readaptation; retained data may still be used to preserve downstream-task utility. Experiments based on the identity-partitioning and one-shot support construction of 1-SHUI show that MCU achieves a favorable empirical trade-off among model utility, membership distinguishability, and request-time computational efficiency compared with the evaluated baselines. These results provide empirical evidence for the potential of controllable external memory in machine unlearning, rather than a formal guarantee of complete information removal.
tldr: Memory-Coupled Unlearning (MCU) augments a host model with a Modern Hopfield Network as external identity-prototype memory to support identity-level machine unlearning when the complete forget set is absent during readaptation.
motivation: Identity-level unlearning is difficult when only limited target-specific information is available at request time and the full original forget set cannot be used for gradient-based readaptation.
method: MCU stores aggregated identity prototypes in a Modern Hopfield Network, uses a Prototype Adaptation Network and Dependency Gating Unit to control memory contribution, and removes the relevant prototype before readapting on limited support information plus retained data.
result: Experiments using 1-SHUI identity partitioning and one-shot support show MCU achieves a favorable empirical trade-off among model utility, membership distinguishability, and request-time computational efficiency compared with baselines.
conclusion: The work provides empirical evidence for controllable external memory in machine unlearning but does not offer formal guarantees of complete information removal.

title: Physical Side-Channel Attacks On Edge LLMs: Extracting Output Tokens And User Prompts
authors: Najeh Alhalawani, Gunes Acar, Zhuoran Liu, Lejla Batina
abstract: ArXiv:2610.14215v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The deployment of large language models (LLMs) on edge devices is largely motivated by privacy concerns over sharing sensitive user data with cloud servers. In this paper, we demonstrate that keeping inference local does not eliminate privacy risks: an adversary with physical access to the device may exploit hardware leakage to recover sensitive information without compromising or modifying the software system. In particular, we present an electromagnetic (EM) side-channel attack targeting LLM inference on edge devices. Targeting LLaMA-3.2-1B-Instruct running on a Raspberry Pi 5, we demonstrate that EM traces collected during inference can leak both generated tokens and user prompts. We propose three attacks under different threat assumptions. First, a profiling attack that identifies generated tokens among 50 medical and privacy-related keywords with 97.2% accuracy on profiled words. Second, a reconstruction attack recovers the model's hidden representations and uses them to predict tokens from the full 128k-token vocabulary, achieving 94.3% accuracy on profiled classes. For unseen words, the correct token is ranked within the first 100 positions of the 128k-token vocabulary in 67% of cases, with a median rank of 54. Finally, we present a hidden-state inversion attack that uses the recovered hidden state to reconstruct user prompts semantically. Our proposed attacks require only passive EM side-channel measurements and a limited number of traces during model training. These results demonstrate that local execution alone may not guarantee the confidentiality of generated tokens and user inputs.
tldr: The paper demonstrates electromagnetic side-channel attacks that recover generated tokens and user prompts from an LLM running locally on an edge device.
motivation: Edge deployment of LLMs is often motivated by privacy, but physical access may still leak sensitive information through hardware side channels.
method: The authors collect electromagnetic traces during inference on a Raspberry Pi 5 running LLaMA-3.2-1B-Instruct and use profiling, reconstruction, and hidden-state inversion attacks.
result: They achieve 97.2% accuracy on profiled keywords, 94.3% accuracy on profiled classes, and recover unseen tokens within the top 100 of a 128k-token vocabulary in 67% of cases.
conclusion: Local execution alone does not guarantee confidentiality of generated tokens or user prompts, highlighting the need for physical side-channel defenses in edge LLM deployment.

title: Predictive Holonomy And Minimal Completion Of Coarse Dynamics

title: Comment On arXiv:2510.21705 "Fundamental Impossibility Of A Superradiant Neutrino Laser" And Comment On arXiv:2510.21692 "Can Bose-Einstein Condensates Enhance Radioactive Decay?"
authors: Ralph G. Devoe
abstract: ArXiv:2610.13967v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that the small value of the neutrino cross-section rules out superradiance in the laboratory.
tldr: The comment argues that the tiny neutrino cross-section makes superradiance in a neutrino laser impossible in the laboratory.
motivation: To respond to recent proposals claiming a superradiant neutrino laser and possible Bose-Einstein-condensate enhancement of radioactive decay.
method: A theoretical comment based on the small value of the neutrino cross-section, ruling out laboratory superradiance.
result: Laboratory neutrino superradiance is shown to be impossible due to the extremely small neutrino interaction cross-section.
conclusion: Proposals for superradiant neutrino lasers or BEC-enhanced decay are not physically viable in laboratory settings.

title: Additional Ionization During Nuclear $\beta^{\pm}$ Decay In Atomic Systems
authors: Alexei M. Frolov
abstract: ArXiv:2610.14109v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: An original method is developed for numerical calculations of probabilities of the bound-free atomic excitations during the nuclear [MATH] decays in actual atoms and ions. To achieve this goal we have derived and tested the closed analytical formulas for the final state probabilities of different excitations in the few-electron atomic systems. This study is the first non-approximate and essentially complete investigation of the atomic bound-free excitations during the nuclear [MATH] decays in atoms.
tldr: The paper develops an analytical method to compute bound-free atomic excitation probabilities during nuclear beta decay in atoms and ions.
motivation: Nuclear beta decay in atomic systems can cause ionization or excitation of the surrounding electrons, and a non-approximate, complete treatment of these bound-free processes was previously lacking.
method: The author derives closed analytical formulas for final-state probabilities of different excitations in few-electron atomic systems and tests them numerically.
result: The method enables numerical calculations of bound-free excitation probabilities, providing the first essentially complete non-approximate investigation of such processes during nuclear beta decay.
conclusion: This work establishes a general analytical and numerical framework for studying atomic ionization and excitation accompanying nuclear beta decay, with potential applications in atomic and nuclear physics.

title: Diverging Paths To Dark-matter Discovery
authors: Simon Allz\'en
abstract: ArXiv:2610.14137v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The scientific discovery of dark matter has been pursued in two very different methodological and epistemic contexts. A microphysical context centered around the laboratory detection of a new particle, and a macrophysical context based on the astronomical identification of a non-luminous gravitating component. The justification for the salience of methodological diversity is that these different methods are complementary ways to discovering aspects of the same entity. The weakly interacting massive particle (WIMP) made this expectation scientifically credible by connecting a particle candidate to a cosmological abundance, experimental searches, and explanations of astronomical phenomena. What happens to this connection when the WIMP loses its central position? I analyze 201,627 NASA Astrophysics Data System records to examine the organization of research following the decline of WIMP prominence. Astrophysics and high-energy physics remain jointly dominant, while WIMP-related mentions decline in both fields and successor candidates receive different degrees of attention. Concept networks show that WIMP-related research remains central across the literature, even as cross-field connections become less concentrated around it. These indicators measure research attention; they do not establish what scientists would accept as a discovery. I interpret the findings through a framework distinguishing constitutive identification, cosmic attribution, explanatory adequacy, and the cross-domain identification needed to connect them. A particle, compact-object population, or gravitational theory can resolve different parts of the inherited problem, and a partial or multicomponent discovery can leave other parts open. 'Diverging paths' describes this branching of possible resolutions.
tldr: A bibliometric and epistemological analysis of how dark matter research has diverged after the decline of WIMP prominence, based on 201,627 NASA ADS records.
motivation: The paper investigates what happens to the methodological and epistemic connections between particle physics and astrophysics when the WIMP loses its central role in dark matter research.
method: The author analyzes over 200,000 NASA Astrophysics Data System records using concept networks and quantitative indicators to track research attention and cross-field connections.
result: Astrophysics and high-energy physics remain jointly dominant, but WIMP-related mentions decline in both fields, successor candidates receive varying attention, and cross-field connections become less concentrated around WIMPs.
conclusion: The study distinguishes constitutive identification, cosmic attribution, explanatory adequacy, and cross-domain identification, framing 'diverging paths' as a branching of possible partial or multicomponent dark matter resolutions.

title: Fast Local Field Calculation In Cascaded Coupled Systems
authors: Isam Ben Soltane, Romain Asso, Matthieu Davy
abstract: ArXiv:2610.14314v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Computing the field within a sub-unit of cascaded systems is a recurring problem in wave physics. It is central to gradient-based inverse design, in situations where only a region of the system is modified while the rest remains fixed. Standard approaches either resimulate the entire cascade at every change, or require a detailed characterization of every surrounding sub-system. Both become impractical when many design iterations are needed. Here, we introduce a hybrid method combining the [MATH]-matrix approach, which propagates fields through cascaded systems, with the Green's function method, which gives the field generated by a source within a characterized system. In this approach, the sub-systems surrounding the region of interest need only be characterized once, after which the local field can be recomputed rapidly for any new configuration. We validate the method on a disordered lossy waveguide, finding excellent agreement with finite-element simulations. We also demonstrate its efficiency on a disordered multimode cavity, where it achieves a fifty-fold speed-up over full-wave simulation and reduces a wideband focusing calculation from eleven hours to ten minutes. This approach opens the way to fast, iterative field calculations in complex systems coupled to their environment, with direct applications to inverse design and wideband wavefront-shaping.
tldr: The paper introduces a hybrid M-matrix/Green's function method for rapidly computing local fields in cascaded wave-physics systems, validated on disordered waveguides and cavities.
motivation: Computing the field in a sub-unit of a cascaded system is costly for iterative inverse design because standard methods require resimulating the full cascade or fully characterizing all surrounding sub-systems.
method: The authors combine the M-matrix approach for field propagation through cascaded systems with the Green's function method for fields generated by sources in characterized systems, enabling rapid recomputation after one-time characterization of surrounding sub-systems.
result: The method agrees excellently with finite-element simulations on a disordered lossy waveguide and achieves a fifty-fold speed-up on a disordered multimode cavity, reducing a wideband focusing calculation from eleven hours to ten minutes.
conclusion: This approach enables fast iterative field calculations in complex systems coupled to their environment, with direct applications to inverse design and wideband wavefront shaping.

title: Yang-Mills Theory In The Multisymplectic Framework
authors: David Villa-Blanco
abstract: ArXiv:2610.14418v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This Master's thesis develops and applies the multisymplectic field-theory framework to (pure) Yang-Mills theory. Building from the geometric foundations of jet bundles and the Poincar\'e-Cartan forms, the work constructs the Lagrangian multisymplectic formalism for first-order field theories, recovering the usual Euler-Lagrange field equations and extending the Poisson brackets of symplectic mechanics to a full graded Lie algebra. It then establishes the Legendre correspondence with the multisymplectic Hamiltonian formalism (in which Hamilton equations are retrieved) including the case of singular Lagrangians (where a constraint algorithm is reproduced). Breaking Lorentz covariance via a Cauchy surface slicing, the thesis then relates the covariant multisymplectic picture to an instantaneous presymplectic (infinite-dimensional) formulation in which the instantaneous De Donder equations and presymplectic brackets are obtained in a compatible way. A comprehensive treatment of symmetries then leads to multisymplectic and instantaneous momentum maps generalizations and to several versions of Noether's theorems. Specializing the formalism to principal-bundle gauge theory, the thesis identifies the multisymplectic configuration space with the bundle of connections, gauge symmetries with symmetries in the multisymplectic language and builds the Yang-Mills Lagrangian. Lastly, among many computations, the standard tensorial Yang-Mills equations and the Bianchi identity in local trivializations are retrieved, Yang-Mills conserved currents and charges are obtained and the graded algebra is derived for a special class of Hamiltonian forms.
tldr: This Master's thesis develops a multisymplectic geometric framework for pure Yang-Mills theory, including Lagrangian and Hamiltonian formalisms, symmetries, and Noether theorems.
motivation: The work aims to extend symplectic mechanics to field theories using multisymplectic geometry, with Yang-Mills theory as a principal application.
method: The thesis employs jet bundles, Poincaré-Cartan forms, Legendre correspondence, Cauchy surface slicing, and principal-bundle gauge theory to construct covariant and instantaneous formulations.
result: It recovers Euler-Lagrange and Hamilton equations, constraint algorithms for singular Lagrangians, Noether theorems, Yang-Mills equations, Bianchi identity, conserved currents and charges, and a graded algebra for Hamiltonian forms.
conclusion: The multisymplectic framework provides a consistent geometric foundation for Yang-Mills theory, bridging covariant and instantaneous descriptions, though it lies outside quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, and hybrid quantum systems.

title: A Portable Optical Frequency Comb With Low Repetition-Rate Drift Based On "Optical Cubes"
authors: Zhendong Chen, Hanbo Xu, Ruoao Yang, Tianyu Liu, Hongshuo Wu, Duo Pan, Zhigang Zhang, Jianjun Wu, Jingbiao Chen
abstract: ArXiv:2610.14490v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We demonstrate a compact, fully stabilized, all-polarization-maintaining (all-PM) Er:fiber optical frequency comb (OFC) implemented on a silica optical-cube platform. The optical comb module, including the oscillator, amplifier, spectral-broadening stage, 780-nm frequency-doubling branch, and f-to-2f interferometer, occupies a volume of 0.88 L. Without active temperature control, the free-running repetition frequency exhibits a peak-to-peak excursion of 75 Hz over 10 h, corresponding to 0.375 ppm. Under the same laboratory conditions, this excursion is 6.2 times smaller than that of a mechanically mounted non-PM reference comb. The amplified pulses are compressed to 94 fs and spectrally broadened in a PM highly nonlinear fiber. A coherent-population-trapping-based chip-scale atomic clock is employed for the first time as the radio-frequency reference for comb locking, thereby reducing the footprint of the microwave-reference subsystem. The resulting in-loop, optical-frequency-normalized tracking instability reaches 6.03E-17 at 1 s and 2.57E-18 at 10,000 s. These results demonstrate a compact comb architecture with reduced sensitivity to environmental perturbations, providing a practical route toward portable optical atomic clocks.
tldr: A compact, fully stabilized all-PM Er:fiber optical frequency comb on a silica optical-cube platform with low repetition-rate drift for portable optical clocks.
motivation: To develop portable optical atomic clocks and precision measurement systems that are robust against environmental perturbations.
method: Integrate the oscillator, amplifier, spectral broadening, 780-nm doubling, and f-to-2f interferometer on optical cubes, using a chip-scale atomic clock as RF reference, and measure in-loop instability.
result: Achieved a repetition-frequency peak-to-peak excursion of 75 Hz over 10 h (0.375 ppm) without active temperature control, and an in-loop instability of 6.03E-17 at 1 s and 2.57E-18 at 10,000 s.
conclusion: The compact comb architecture reduces sensitivity to environmental perturbations, providing a practical route toward portable optical atomic clocks.

title: Null-controllable Data For Cascade Heat Equations: Almost Sharp Spectral Spaces And Modal Critical Times
authors: Hugo Lhachemi (L2S), Christophe Prieur (gipsa-Infinity), Emmanuel Tr\'elat

title: A Splitting Proximal Method In Portfolio Optimization With Entropic Value-at-risk
authors: Nail Baloul, Sorin-Mihai Grad, Oleg Wilfer
abstract: ArXiv:2610.14364v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Motivated by a recent paper where a convex portfolio optimization problem formulated by means of the entropic value-at-risk is solved via a primal-dual interior-point method, we propose an alternative way of dealing with such problems by means of splitting proximal point methods and making use of Lagrange duality. Numerical experiments where the new method is implemented for solving some portfolio optimization problems are presented as well. As byproducts, we also provide formulae for the projection on the epigraph of the weighted Shannon entropy, and the conjugate function and subdifferential of entropic value-at-risk.
tldr: The paper proposes a splitting proximal point method for convex portfolio optimization problems formulated with entropic value-at-risk.
motivation: Motivated by prior interior-point approaches to such portfolio problems, the authors seek an alternative optimization method using splitting and duality.
method: They apply splitting proximal point methods and Lagrange duality, and derive formulas for the projection onto the epigraph of weighted Shannon entropy and the conjugate function and subdifferential of entropic value-at-risk.
result: Numerical experiments demonstrate the implementation of the new method on some portfolio optimization problems.
conclusion: The work provides an alternative computational approach and useful byproduct formulas, but it has no connection to quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Dimension-independent Eigenvalue Approximation For Sparse Matrices
authors: Natalia Hajlasz, Christopher Musco, Jonathan Weare, Robert J. Webber
abstract: ArXiv:2610.14620v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Many applications in science and engineering require solving sparse Hermitian eigenvalue problems that are so large that even algorithms whose runtime scales linearly with the matrix dimension are unacceptably slow. Responding to this challenge, there is a growing body of work on sparsified iterative methods and submatrix selection methods that often perform well in practice. However, theoretical understanding of these methods is limited. In this paper, we take a step toward better understanding sublinear-time eigenvalue computation by analyzing the sparsified power method. We prove that the method approximates a leading eigenpair to a prescribed accuracy in a number of iterations comparable to the standard power method. The required number of retained nonzeros depends explicitly on the target accuracy, the initial overlap with the leading eigenvector, the compressibility of the leading eigenvector, and the relative spectral gap. When these quantities and the column sparsity are independent of dimension, the runtime is independent of dimension. In contrast, we show that a comparable worst-case guarantee cannot hold for a prototypical sparsified submatrix selection method. Submatrix selection is the approach of choice in many quantum chemistry applications. However, we show that, even with substantial initial eigenvector overlap, a single iteration of the method can produce a vector that is orthogonal to the leading eigenvector, after which the method cannot recover. Nevertheless, experiments on matrices from the SuiteSparse matrix collection and quantum chemistry problems illustrate the practical effectiveness of submatrix selection methods in a variety of domains despite these worst-case limitations.
tldr: The paper analyzes a sparsified power method for sublinear-time approximation of leading eigenpairs of sparse Hermitian matrices and contrasts it with submatrix selection methods.
motivation: Large sparse Hermitian eigenvalue problems are common in science and engineering, and existing sparsified iterative and submatrix selection methods lack strong theoretical guarantees.
method: The authors prove convergence and sparsity guarantees for the sparsified power method, with runtime depending on accuracy, initial overlap, compressibility, spectral gap, and column sparsity, and they construct a worst-case counterexample for submatrix selection.
result: The sparsified power method can be dimension-independent when relevant quantities and column sparsity are dimension-independent, while submatrix selection can fail catastrophically even with substantial initial overlap.
conclusion: Despite worst-case limitations, experiments on SuiteSparse and quantum chemistry matrices show submatrix selection remains practically effective.

title: Assortment Optimization Under The Mallows Model: Independent-Utility Choice Equivalence And Its Algorithmic Implications
authors: Danny Segev
abstract: ArXiv:2610.14329v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Mallows model is a well-established construct in preference modeling, describing random rankings through their Kendall-Tau distance from a reference permutation. Its compact parameterization and interpretable treatment of preference uncertainty have made it influential across statistics, machine learning, probability, and revenue management. In the latter domain, recent literature has studied the embedding of Mallows-driven choice into assortment optimization. Early approximation schemes in this context require stylized structural simplifications or restrictive parametric assumptions. In the absence of these levers, a highly involved quasi-polynomial-time approximation scheme has subsequently been proposed, leaving wide open the question of whether near-optimal assortments can be computed in true polynomial time. The main contribution of this focused technical paper resides in closing these gaps by uncovering a striking independent-utility structure within Mallows choices, and turning this representation into a polynomial-time approximation scheme. Our central structural characterization explicitly constructs a single collection of mutually independent utilities, reproducing Mallows choice probabilities simultaneously for all offered sets. This exact choice equivalence connects pending Mallows-related challenges to the recent approximation framework of Bowers et al. (FOCS 2025) for assortment optimization under independent random utilities. We make this connection algorithmically feasible through a finite-support reduction that produces distributions of polynomial size while controlling revenue loss uniformly over all assortments. Fused together, these ingredients lead to an [MATH]-time approximation scheme for assortment optimization under the Mallows model, while allowing arbitrary product prices, concentration parameters, and modal rankings.
tldr: This paper establishes an exact independent-utility choice equivalence for Mallows choice models and uses it to develop a polynomial-time approximation scheme for assortment optimization.
motivation: The Mallows model is widely used for preference rankings, but prior assortment optimization approximations required restrictive assumptions or quasi-polynomial time, leaving open whether near-optimal assortments can be computed in polynomial time.
method: The paper constructs a collection of mutually independent utilities that reproduces Mallows choice probabilities for all offered sets, reduces this to polynomial-size finite-support distributions, and connects the problem to the approximation framework of Bowers et al. (FOCS 2025).
result: It obtains a polynomial-time approximation scheme for assortment optimization under the Mallows model with arbitrary product prices, concentration parameters, and modal rankings.
conclusion: The structural equivalence bridges pending Mallows-related challenges to independent-utility assortment optimization and enables efficient approximation in a previously open setting.

title: StateSync-GKR: Design And Evaluation Of A Reusable Sparse Gkr Engine
authors: Jinwook Kim
abstract: ArXiv:2610.14849v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Authenticated state transitions need proof engines that conserve memory, avoid repeated setup, and preserve request semantics across parallel execution. We present StateSync-GKR, a reusable Rust sumcheck/GKR core with a sparse-Merkle frontend, and connect its design mechanisms to controlled measurements. Sparse layer reduction and derived wiring reduce prover ownership and repeated verification work. Cube/affine fusion and parallel path constraints keep the circuit schedule and proof-size growth compact. Reusable preparation and indexed parallel jobs amortize setup while maintaining independent results. Three-state records, strict original-request decoding, and separate core/model interfaces expose the application and assurance boundaries. With circuit, field, transcript and prover driver held fixed, sparse reduction lowers additional requested allocation 3,242-fold and peak process resident memory 89.46-fold relative to StateSync-GKR's test-only dense reference for a two-layer mixed circuit of width 4096. Direct depth-24 fresh/prepared measurements show 3.46-4.45-fold lower per-request proving-path latency. CPU and full-proof delivery studies distinguish useful parallel work from queueing and return-path costs, retaining all outcomes and latency budgets. The evaluation supports larger circuits within finite RAM, lower repeated-request cost, and explicit deployment choices for this artifact. It preserves the cryptographic claim boundary of the existing construction.
tldr: Presents StateSync-GKR, a reusable Rust sumcheck/GKR proof engine with a sparse-Merkle frontend, and evaluates its memory and latency improvements for authenticated state transitions.
motivation: Authenticated state transitions need proof engines that conserve memory, avoid repeated setup, and preserve request semantics across parallel execution.
method: The work implements sparse layer reduction, derived wiring, cube/affine fusion, parallel path constraints, reusable preparation, and indexed parallel jobs, then evaluates them with circuit, field, transcript, and prover driver held fixed.
result: Sparse reduction lowers additional requested allocation 3,242-fold and peak process resident memory 89.46-fold relative to a dense reference, while depth-24 fresh/prepared measurements show 3.46–4.45-fold lower per-request proving-path latency.
conclusion: The evaluation supports larger circuits within finite RAM and lower repeated-request cost, providing explicit deployment choices while preserving the cryptographic claim boundary of the existing construction.

title: Energy, Passivity, And Diffusive Representations In Anisotropic Fractional Maxwell--Cole--Cole Media
authors: Nikko John Leo S. Lobos
abstract: ArXiv:2610.13985v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This study develops an energy formulation for linear anisotropic Maxwell--Cole--Cole media with multiple fractional polarization channels, passive conductivity, prescribed currents, and finite-terminal Caputo memory with zero prehistory. A weighted solution class captures the integrable fractional initial layer generated by quiescent polarization. Fractional polarization power then separates into a nonnegative history storage and a nonnegative constitutive dissipation rate. Although the instantaneous rate may diverge at initialization, it remains integrable, while stored history energy and accumulated loss vanish initially. Combined with the Poynting theorem, this decomposition yields a global field-plus-memory identity that establishes electromagnetic passivity, closed-system energy decay, and conditional uniqueness under zero-supply boundary conditions. The framework also recovers the Debye, instantaneous-dielectric, vanishing-susceptibility, and vacuum limits under convergence assumptions. A positive diffusive representation provides a second decomposition whose storage never exceeds the history storage. Their difference is an exact nonnegative weighted variance that vanishes only for a zero polarization history. In agreement with these time-domain results, the finite-time harmonic response approaches the anisotropic multichannel Cole--Cole permittivity, whose Hermitian imaginary part ensures nonnegative cycle-averaged absorption. A reproducible single-channel study shows that fractional order broadens the dielectric-loss band, redistributes wave attenuation, strengthens the integrable initial power layer, and prolongs the step-response tail. An exact electric-step response verifies both energy representations. The formulation connects fractional initial layers, hereditary storage, passivity, diffusive relaxation, dispersion, absorption, and attenuation in a local constitutive model.
tldr: The paper formulates energy storage and dissipation for anisotropic fractional Maxwell–Cole–Cole media, proving electromagnetic passivity and exact diffusive representations.
motivation: Fractional dielectric relaxation models are widely used but lack a complete energy formulation connecting memory, passivity, and dispersion in anisotropic multichannel media.
method: The authors define a weighted solution class for Caputo fractional evolution with zero prehistory, decompose fractional polarization power into history storage and constitutive dissipation, and combine it with Poynting's theorem and harmonic analysis.
result: They obtain global field-plus-memory energy identities, passivity and decay, conditional uniqueness, limit recoveries, a positive diffusive representation with nonnegative variance, and a single-channel numerical study of loss-band broadening and attenuation redistribution.
conclusion: The framework unifies fractional initial layers, hereditary storage, passivity, diffusive relaxation, and absorption in a local constitutive model for anisotropic fractional Maxwell–Cole–Cole media.

title: A Gauge-Inspired Coupled Fokker--Planck System For Multistate Stochastic Dynamics: Formalism And 1-d Numerical Implementation
authors: Francesco Pio de Cosmo, Gianluca Di Natale, Leandro Cieri
abstract: ArXiv:2610.14052v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Extending the Fokker--Planck equation to a coupled system of equations through non-Abelian symmetry groups offers a powerful theoretical framework for coupled multi-state stochastic systems. However, translating this abstract gauge field formulation into viable numerical predictions remains an unaddressed challenge. Motivated by our previous work on ice crystal habit evolution, in this work we bridge this gap by presenting the first numerical solver for an SU(2) gauge-coupled Fokker--Planck system in (1+1) dimensions. Using an operator-splitting scheme combined with a non-oscillatory advection solver, our algorithm strictly ensures probability conservation, non-negativity, and numerical stability. We demonstrate that non-Abelian gauge coupling acts as a cross-reactive feedback loop that fundamentally alters system dynamics, driving continuous probability exchange between states, suppressing localised density peaks, and forcing long-time spatial delocalisation. Validated across linear and quadratic coupling regimes up to strong interactions (g <= 1.0), this work establishes the foundational computational infrastructure needed to integrate complex multi-state physics. Overall, while our approach provides a key step toward improving ice cloud representation in atmospheric and climate models, the underlying physical framework and computational engine remain fundamentally general and multidisciplinary, offering a versatile paradigm for any domain requiring coupled multi-state stochastic equations.
tldr: The paper presents a numerical solver for an SU(2) gauge-coupled Fokker-Planck system to model multistate stochastic dynamics, motivated by ice crystal habit evolution.
motivation: Extending the Fokker-Planck equation via non-Abelian gauge symmetries offers a theoretical framework for coupled multi-state stochastic systems, but numerical implementations were lacking.
method: An operator-splitting scheme combined with a non-oscillatory advection solver is developed for the SU(2) gauge-coupled Fokker-Planck system in (1+1) dimensions, ensuring probability conservation, non-negativity, and stability.
result: The non-Abelian gauge coupling induces continuous probability exchange between states, suppresses localized density peaks, and forces long-time spatial delocalization, validated for linear and quadratic coupling up to strong interactions.
conclusion: The work provides a general computational infrastructure for coupled multistate stochastic dynamics, with potential applications in atmospheric/climate modeling and other domains, but it is not directly related to quantum information or quantum thermodynamics.

title: Joint Trust-Distrust Structure Shapes Belief Propagation And Collective Dynamics
authors: Yu-Ru Lin Mozhgan Khanjanianpak
abstract: ArXiv:2610.14565v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Belief propagation in social networks depends on how trust and distrust jointly shape interpersonal influence. We develop a network model that treats trust and distrust as distinct but statistically coupled quantities. Their joint values determine the net trust and uncertainty of each relationship, and a neighbor can influence an agent only when both threshold conditions are satisfied. We show that the correlation between trust and distrust reshapes the transition between consensus and fragmentation by changing the availability of influential neighbors. Network connectivity also affects this transition, whereas degree heterogeneity has a more limited effect when networks have comparable mean degree. Moreover, the availability of influential neighbors alone does not determine the final consensus: correlations between relational properties and network degree can select agents with different degree compositions, altering the direction and magnitude of collective belief. Finally, we introduce a comfort index that quantifies the expected availability of influential neighbors and analytically links the joint trust-distrust structure to collective dynamics. Our results establish a mechanistic connection between relational structure, effective social influence, and emergent collective belief states.
tldr: A network model shows how the joint trust-distrust structure and degree correlations shape consensus versus fragmentation in social belief propagation.
motivation: Belief propagation in social networks depends on how trust and distrust jointly influence interpersonal interactions, but their coupled effects on collective dynamics remain unclear.
method: The authors develop a network model where trust and distrust are distinct but correlated, and influence occurs only when both threshold conditions are satisfied; they analyze how correlations, connectivity, and degree heterogeneity affect consensus transitions.
result: Trust-distrust correlations reshape the consensus-fragmentation transition by changing the availability of influential neighbors, and correlations with network degree can bias collective belief direction and magnitude.
conclusion: A comfort index links joint trust-distrust structure to collective dynamics, establishing a mechanistic connection between relational structure, effective social influence, and emergent belief states.

title: Selective Spatiotemporal Mode-locking In Multimode Mamyshev Oscillators
authors: Changfeng Wang, Jia Liu, Yutai Zhao, Ran Xia, Wenjun Ni, Chunyong Yang, Xiahui Tang, Gang Xu, Perry Ping Shum
abstract: ArXiv:2610.14690v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Spatiotemporal mode-locking (STML) in multimode fibers introduces spatial degrees of freedom for ultrashort pulse generation, yet flexible manipulation of transverse mode compositions within multimode solitons remains challenging. Here, we propose a spectrum-to-mode mapping strategy in multimode Mamyshev oscillators (MOs) to selectively synchronize specific transverse modes through synergistic cross-phase modulation and offset spectral filtering. Meanwhile, four-wave mixing acts to stabilize intermodal phase relationships, facilitating selective STML characterized by diverse mode compositions with matched group velocities. Spatiotemporal solitons containing the pure LP01 mode, degenerate LP11 modes, or LP02+LP21 composite modes are selectively realized and mapped across the parameter space spanned by intracavity gain and filter detuning. Furthermore, intracavity collisions between coexisting mode groups with disparate group velocities are demonstrated to enable dynamic mode selection. Beyond the simulation of six modes in graded-index multimode fibers, selective STML is also demonstrated in MOs based on step-index multimode fibers and fibers supporting more transverse modes, confirming the generality of our approach. This strategy offers a versatile and robust pathway for transverse mode regulation and provides new insights into full dimensional structured light manipulation in multimode ultrafast fiber lasers.
tldr: This paper proposes a spectrum-to-mode mapping strategy for selective spatiotemporal mode-locking in multimode Mamyshev oscillators to control transverse mode compositions.
motivation: Flexible manipulation of transverse mode compositions within multimode solitons remains challenging despite the introduction of spatial degrees of freedom by spatiotemporal mode-locking.
method: The authors use synergistic cross-phase modulation and offset spectral filtering to selectively synchronize transverse modes, with four-wave mixing stabilizing intermodal phase relationships, and demonstrate the approach through simulations in graded-index and step-index multimode fibers.
result: Selective spatiotemporal solitons containing pure LP01, degenerate LP11, or LP02+LP21 composite modes are realized across intracavity gain and filter detuning parameter space, and dynamic mode selection via intracavity collisions is demonstrated.
conclusion: The strategy offers a versatile and robust pathway for transverse mode regulation and provides new insights into full-dimensional structured light manipulation in multimode ultrafast fiber lasers.
