A feasible rank-one beam can therefore be compared directly with the optimum of the finite-scenario problem. We also derive a precision-weighted linear predictor that suppresses uncertain physical-velocity estimates after observation-frame transport. Paired dynamic simulations reduce direction-cosine RMSE by 51.29\% relative to unrestricted nine-point extrapolation. In a separate uncertainty experiment, direct rate optimization increases mean minimum spectral efficiency from 0.32425 to 0.41712 bit/s/Hz, an improvement of 28.64\%; the corresponding design objective is within [MATH] bit/s/Hz of a global upper bound. The phase-transport equation fixes a coherent representative of each optimal beam without changing its gain.
tldr: The paper optimizes receive designs for RSMA satellite-UAV downlinks using a physical-observation dual-axis framework, including matched combiners, beamforming under uncertainty, and rate optimization.
motivation: Receiver observation state can differ from physical signal state, motivating separate receive-beam design and phase-reference transport in RSMA satellite-UAV links.
method: The authors formulate receive optimization in a physical-observation dual-axis (PODA) structure, derive noise-weighted matched combiners and principal eigenvector beamforming, and use semidefinite relaxation for rate optimization.
result: Simulations show 51.29% reduction in direction-cosine RMSE and a 28.64% increase in mean minimum spectral efficiency, with the design objective near a global upper bound.
conclusion: The proposed receive design improves robustness and rate performance for RSMA satellite-UAV downlinks under directional and velocity uncertainty.

title: Algorithms With Smoothed Polynomial-Time Complexity For Deterministic Discounted-sum And Mean-payoff Games
authors: Ali Asadi, Krishnendu Chatterjee, Ruichen Luo
abstract: ArXiv:2610.14150v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Turn-based deterministic games on graphs are two-player zero-sum games played on finite directed graphs, where the vertex set is partitioned between the Max and the adversarial Min Player. The respective player chooses outgoing edges from their vertices. We consider these games with the classical discounted-sum and mean-payoff objectives. The goal of the Max Player is to maximize the objective against the adversarial Min Player. These games lie in NP [MATH] coNP and are among the rare combinatorial problems that belong to this complexity class, yet the existence of a polynomial-time algorithm is a major open question. All known deterministic algorithms require exponential time in the worst case, while the classical strategy iteration (policy iteration) algorithm is remarkably efficient in practice, which motivates the study of the smoothed complexity of these games. Previous results established a smoothed polynomial-time bound only for the restricted class of ergodic games and presented only a high-probability guarantee. Our main result is a new analysis technique for a variant of the strategy iteration algorithm, and we show these algorithms achieve smoothed polynomial complexity for general game graphs with both high-probability and expected runtime guarantees. In particular, our result removes the ergodicity restriction of prior work and strengthens the high-probability guarantee to the stronger expected-runtime guarantee, thereby resolving the open question on the smoothed complexity of these games.
tldr: The paper develops smoothed polynomial-time complexity guarantees for a variant of strategy iteration applied to deterministic discounted-sum and mean-payoff games, removing the ergodicity restriction of prior work.
motivation: Deterministic discounted-sum and mean-payoff games lie in NP ∩ coNP, but no polynomial-time algorithm is known; strategy iteration is efficient in practice, motivating smoothed complexity analysis beyond the restricted ergodic case.
method: The authors introduce a new analysis technique for a variant of the strategy iteration algorithm and prove smoothed polynomial complexity for general game graphs with both high-probability and expected-runtime guarantees.
result: The algorithm achieves smoothed polynomial complexity for general game graphs, strengthening prior high-probability bounds to expected-runtime bounds and eliminating the ergodicity assumption.
conclusion: This resolves the open question on the smoothed complexity of discounted-sum and mean-payoff games, advancing algorithmic game theory but having no direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Embedding Asymmetry As Attack Signal: Detecting And Defending Active Label Inference In Vertical Federated Learning
authors: Muhammad Abdullah Adnan Soumya Swagata Biswas
abstract: ArXiv:2610.14194v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Vertical federated learning lets organizations train a shared model over features they hold separately, while one party keeps the labels private. The active label inference attack of Fu et al. [12] breaks this: a feature-holding party runs a modified optimizer, MaliciousSGD, that forces class structure into its embeddings and then recovers the labels with semi-supervised learning. Defenses that perturb the shared gradient fail, because the attack acts on the party's internal optimizer, not on the message it sends. We show the attack leaves a signal the server can read from the embeddings it already receives. The adversary's Fisher class-separability pulls away from the honest party's, and the gap is visible within a few epochs. A defense triggered by this signal acts on the adversary alone. Scaling its gradient down handles few-class tasks, and a norm non-expansive projection handles many-class tasks, with the Discriminative Coverage Ratio explaining why the projection rank must grow with the class count. The defense breaks the alignment between embedding clusters and labels rather than destroying the embedding. Across four seeds on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and CINIC-10, label inference falls below what honest training already leaks, at under two points of task-accuracy cost.
tldr: The paper detects and defends active label inference attacks in vertical federated learning by exploiting asymmetry in embedding Fisher class-separability.
motivation: Vertical federated learning aims to protect label privacy, but the MaliciousSGD attack breaks it by manipulating a party's local optimizer; existing gradient-perturbation defenses fail because the attack is internal.
method: The server monitors embeddings for a Fisher class-separability gap between the adversary and honest party, then applies an adversary-specific defense: gradient scaling for few-class tasks or a norm non-expansive projection for many-class tasks.
result: Across four seeds on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and CINIC-10, label inference falls below the level of honest training leakage, with under two points of task-accuracy cost.
conclusion: Embedding asymmetry provides a practical signal for detecting and defending active label inference in vertical federated learning without harming honest parties.

title: Armor: Adversary Cost Amplification Via A Schema-Preserving Password-Hardening Retrofit For Resource-Constrained Systems
authors: Avinash Srinivasan
abstract: ArXiv:2610.14300v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Internet of Things (IoT) gateways, edge authentication servers, and legacy systems need protection against offline password guessing after credential-database disclosure. Memory-hard key derivation functions (KDFs) are the preferred defense, but their resource requirements can exceed memory or latency budgets. ARMOR addresses this gap with a schema-preserving verifier-side transform for database-only (DB-only) compromise. Secret per-account chains of injective operations reside in an isolated Chain Registry. Fixed terminal escape encoding preserves distinct pre-hash values under each chain and moves outputs outside printable ASCII. We evaluate NAIVE adversaries using unmodified cracking tools and AWARE adversaries that enumerate chains. For the evaluated pre-hardened three-operation chains, NAIVE recovery is at most 0.10% on non-digit targets. Escape encoding yields zero recovery of digit-only targets under evaluated stock rule-based and non-rule attacks, closing a bypass permitting up to 45.3% recovery. Across 14.05 million eligible RockYou password entries, retaining duplicates, the median conditional guessing number is approximately 52 output-class tests at depth three and 317 at depth five. These values quantify the chain-search subproblem given the correct plaintext under a unit-cost model. A separate historical 14-operation AWARE evaluation matches all transformed targets at full dictionary coverage. Deployment measurements show microsecond-scale bare-metal transforms on three IoT boards, with protected storage dominating the measured TrustZone-M prototype components. Although an isolated high-entropy pepper provides stronger cryptographic protection, ARMOR combines compact per-account chain storage with low transform cost. When resources permit and the KDF accepts the complete transformed output, ARMOR composes as KDF(ARMOR(password)).
tldr: ARMOR is a verifier-side, schema-preserving password-hardening transform that uses secret per-account operation chains to amplify offline guessing costs for resource-constrained systems.
motivation: IoT gateways and legacy authentication servers need protection against offline password guessing after credential-database disclosure, but memory-hard key derivation functions may exceed available memory or latency budgets.
method: The scheme stores secret per-account chains of injective operations in an isolated Chain Registry, applies fixed terminal escape encoding to preserve distinct pre-hash values, and can compose with a KDF as KDF(ARMOR(password)).
result: NAIVE recovery is at most 0.10% on non-digit targets, escape encoding yields zero recovery for digit-only targets in evaluated settings, and median conditional guessing numbers are about 52 output-class tests at depth three and 317 at depth five across RockYou entries.
conclusion: ARMOR provides compact per-account chain storage with low transform cost on IoT boards, offering a practical retrofit when resources do not permit stronger cryptographic protection such as an isolated high-entropy pepper.

title: Natural Code Transformation Confuses Agents In Vulnerability Analysis
authors: Jie Zhu, Ronik Bhaskar, Heather Zheng, Ben Y. Zhao, Kexin Pei
abstract: ArXiv:2610.14350v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Having demonstrated a strong potential for automating vulnerability discovery, AI agents can also be used to attack software systems at scale. Today's software systems need mechanisms to level the playing field by slowing down potential attacks, giving them time to patch vulnerabilities and strengthen software. Along this line, our study of agent trajectories in vulnerability analysis shows a surprising finding: agents produce dramatically different results across real-world code commits that carry the same functionality and the same vulnerability. This phenomenon appears consistently in multiple code domains and vulnerability categories. It motivates us to study natural and functionality-preserving code transformations derived from real-world software development, and their potential as a defense against attacker agents. We build a corpus of natural transformations by mining recurring development patterns from real-world code commits, and apply them to evaluate impact on agentic vulnerability analysis. Our results show that even a single form of transformation can effectively "confuse" frontier agents, e.g., Codex with GPT-6 Sol, reducing successes in vulnerability discovery. We also study different agent failures, whether transformations can be composed to provide stronger protection, and adaptive attackers who seek to reverse them. Overall, our study of natural code transformation significantly expands the research space of using code transformations to defend against malicious agents.
tldr: Natural functionality-preserving code transformations can confuse AI agents performing vulnerability analysis, reducing their success in discovering vulnerabilities.
motivation: AI agents can automate vulnerability discovery and be used for attacks, so software systems need defenses that slow attackers and give defenders time to patch.
method: The authors mine recurring development patterns from real-world code commits to build a corpus of natural transformations, then evaluate their impact on agentic vulnerability analysis across multiple domains and vulnerability categories.
result: Even a single transformation can effectively confuse frontier agents such as Codex with GPT-6 Sol, reducing vulnerability discovery success; composing transformations and adaptive attackers are also studied.
conclusion: Natural code transformation expands the research space for defending against malicious AI agents in vulnerability analysis, though it is unrelated to quantum information science.

title: Dice: Tilting The Odds Through Interface Attackson System One Model
authors: Ben Dong, Tianyi Lu, Zhonghao Guo, Qian Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2610.14404v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: System One models offer typed judgments that applications can turn into decisions. Their answers, however, are conditional on the state and question supplied by surrounding components, and on how the application uses the response. We study this boundary in a Jev-based pipeline with bounded substitutions at three adapter outputs: state extraction, question generation, and output interpretation. Across three small synthetic studies, each adapter can change the final decision while Jev and its authentic API responses remain outside attacker control. The cases expose distinct failures of source fidelity, answer meaning, and response relevance. Checks that bind these relationships stopped the corresponding interventions we tested, although source verification also rejected some valid clean decisions. The pilot identifies where correct request-level judgments can lose their connection to the original task; it does not estimate the prevalence of these failures in deployed systems.
tldr: This paper studies interface attacks on System One models in a Jev-based pipeline, showing that bounded substitutions at adapter outputs can alter final decisions without compromising the underlying model or authentic API responses.
motivation: System One models provide typed judgments used by applications, but their outputs depend on surrounding components including state extraction, question generation, and output interpretation, creating potential attack surfaces at component boundaries.
method: The authors conduct three small synthetic studies with bounded substitutions at three adapter outputs—state extraction, question generation, and output interpretation—within a Jev-based pipeline.
result: Each adapter can change the final decision while Jev and its authentic API responses remain outside attacker control, exposing failures in source fidelity, answer meaning, and response relevance; checks binding these relationships stopped the tested interventions but also rejected some valid clean decisions.
conclusion: The pilot identifies where correct request-level judgments can lose connection to the original task, but it does not estimate the prevalence of these failures in deployed systems.

title: Beyond Independent Values: Optimal Auctions With Correlated Valuations For LLM-Native Advertising
authors: Mingyu Guo Shiman Sheng
abstract: ArXiv:2610.14646v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Conversational assistants are becoming the place where people ask what to buy, and sponsored content is moving into their answers. Several advertisers then compete for one sponsored slot, and all of them read the same conversation, so their willingness to pay usually moves together. Existing auctions for LLM advertising treat these values as independent. We therefore present AffMyerson, an auction that captures this correlation and turns it into revenue. We model the advertisers' values given the conversation as a multivariate normal and turn the economic premise of positive dependence (affiliation) into a sign condition on the precision matrix. We design a neural parameterization whose every output satisfies it. We prove that every prior in this family yields a truthful, ex-post individually rational auction, so estimation error can cost revenue but never truthfulness. We derive the conditional virtual values in closed form. By the design of the prior, pricing an auction needs no matrix inversion and takes O(n^2) time, fast enough to run at query time. We also work out the log-normal family used in empirical ad-auction work. There we prove that the auction is truthful for every prior and revenue-optimal when the prior is correct, and that the virtual value is regular everywhere whenever the conditional spread is below a loose threshold, which our fitted priors stay well under. With LLM-agent bidders, AffMyerson earns 6.2% more than a second-price auction with a tuned reserve, 6.1% more than Ronen's lookahead auction with the same prior, and 9.2% more than Myerson's auction run as if values were independent. This gain is still 4.5% on real keyword search queries where willingness to pay is hard to read. The correlation comes from common demand. Agents that judge the conversation bid together and agents told to calculate do not. The gain from conditioning moves with the correlation.
tldr: The paper proposes AffMyerson, a truthful auction mechanism for LLM-native advertising that exploits correlated advertiser valuations to improve revenue over independent-value benchmarks.
motivation: Existing auctions for LLM advertising treat advertiser values as independent, ignoring correlation arising from shared conversation context.
method: Models advertiser values as multivariate normal/log-normal with positive dependence, designs neural parameterization and closed-form conditional virtual values, proving truthfulness and ex-post individual rationality.
result: AffMyerson earns 6.2% more than second-price with tuned reserve, 6.1% more than Ronen's lookahead auction, 9.2% more than independent Myerson, with 4.5% gain on real keyword search queries.
conclusion: Exploiting correlated valuations in LLM ad auctions yields practical revenue gains while preserving truthfulness and computational efficiency.

title: No, Your Tools Are Not Enough: It's Time To Bring Agents To The Hunt
authors: Ati Priya Bajaj, Xiang Mei, Tiffany Bao, Yan Shoshitaishvili, Ruoyu Wang, Adam Doup\'e
abstract: ArXiv:2610.14729v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Modern software systems are large and complex, demanding scalable and autonomous techniques for vulnerability discovery. Existing approaches still depend on human expertise for domain knowledge, and on human intervention throughout the process of vulnerability discovery. AI agents offer us an opportunity to make vulnerability discovery more adaptive, scalable, and autonomous. Agents bring the ability to make continuous decisions and adapt, and general knowledge that can be augmented. In this paper, we present our experience using AI agents to find vulnerabilities across diverse programs such as Windows drivers, the Linux kernel, XNU, firmware, and web applications. We use an iterative agentic workflow and find that it generalizes across these targets. We discuss tasks that agents help with, which were previously challenging, and some future research directions we consider important for advancing autonomous vulnerability discovery.
tldr: The paper reports experience using AI agents for autonomous vulnerability discovery across diverse software targets.
motivation: Modern software systems are complex and existing vulnerability discovery approaches still rely heavily on human expertise and intervention, motivating more scalable and autonomous techniques.
method: The authors employ an iterative agentic workflow and apply it to find vulnerabilities in Windows drivers, the Linux kernel, XNU, firmware, and web applications.
result: The agentic workflow generalizes across the tested targets and helps with tasks that were previously challenging for automated tools.
conclusion: AI agents can make vulnerability discovery more adaptive, scalable, and autonomous, and the paper outlines future research directions for advancing this area.

title: StructHCP: Structure-Aware Sat--cegar For The Hamiltonian Cycle Problem
authors: Quan van Vi, Tuyen van Kieu, Khanh van To
abstract: ArXiv:2610.14780v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Many exact Hamiltonian-cycle solvers use the same edge-level representation for every input, even when graph structure admits a smaller set of global decisions. We present StructHCP, a SAT--CEGAR pipeline that selects a representation through inexpensive structural recognizers. Specialized searches handle high-degree clusters and paired chains, while complete directed and undirected encodings handle cubic and general graphs. Every returned cycle is reconstructed when necessary and verified in the input graph. On the 1,001-instance FHCP Challenge Set, StructHCP solves 826 instances, compared with 741 when the same general SAT--CEGAR engine is applied directly to every unreduced input graph. Relative to this ablation, StructHCP reduces PAR-2 by 32.9 percent. Formulation selection solves 82 more instances than the contracted general encoding; high-degree-cluster and cubic graphs account for 81 of this difference. StructHCP also solves 34 of the 51 instances solved by neither HCup nor Cut-set CEGAR, raising the combined coverage of the three solvers from 950 to 984. Twelve of its solutions lie outside the union of published per-instance SAT results analyzed here, and six also lie outside the published exact result sets in our comparison. These results show that selecting the representation can complement connectivity refinement on structured HCP instances.
tldr: StructHCP is a structure-aware SAT-CEGAR pipeline that selects graph-specific encodings to solve the Hamiltonian Cycle Problem more efficiently than a general SAT-CEGAR engine.
motivation: Exact Hamiltonian-cycle solvers typically use a single edge-level representation, even when graph structure permits smaller global decisions, leaving performance gains unrealized.
method: The authors use inexpensive structural recognizers to select specialized searches for high-degree clusters and paired chains, or complete directed/undirected encodings for cubic and general graphs, with cycle reconstruction and verification.
result: On the 1,001-instance FHCP Challenge Set, StructHCP solves 826 instances versus 741 for the direct general SAT-CEGAR ablation, reducing PAR-2 by 32.9% and solving 34 instances missed by HCup and Cut-set CEGAR.
conclusion: Representation selection complements connectivity refinement for structured HCP instances and improves overall exact solver coverage.

title: MetaCascade: End-to-End Attacks On Agent Skills Via Metadata-Only Poisoning
authors: Junhao Wen, Ping Deng, Qizhi Chen, Junchen Li, Shuang Liang
abstract: ArXiv:2610.14836v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As a key extension mechanism for agent systems, Agent Skills package specialized capabilities for reuse by LLM agents. An agent first retrieves candidate skills based on skill documentation and then relies on their metadata to make the final selection. As third-party skills proliferate on insufficiently vetted open registry platforms, the security risks posed by malicious skills become increasingly prominent, but existing attack research still focuses primarily on the potential harm caused after their execution. The limited related studies typically examine skill retrieval or selection in isolation and have yet to cover a complete end-to-end attack chain. To address this research gap, we find an end-to-end attack surface arising from the process-wide influence of metadata. Based on this finding, we propose MetaCascade, an end-to-end metadata-only poisoning framework. MetaCascade first generates diverse malicious skill candidates through multi-view semantic expansion, then uses tasks and black-box competition feedback to analyze the competitive relationships among malicious candidate skills and iteratively optimize malicious metadata, thereby improving the target skill's end-to-end attack effectiveness. Under a unified evaluation setting spanning four datasets and two agents, Hermes and OpenClaw, MetaCascade achieves state-of-the-art attack performance, with its average attack success rate (ASR) and its average ASR under four defense settings exceeding the strongest baselines under the corresponding settings by 35.53 and 34.65 percentage points, respectively. Our code is provided in the supplementary material.
tldr: MetaCascade is an end-to-end metadata-only poisoning framework that attacks LLM agent skills by optimizing malicious skill metadata to improve retrieval and selection.
motivation: Agent Skills on open registry platforms pose security risks, but existing attacks focus mainly on post-execution harm and do not cover the full end-to-end attack chain.
method: The framework generates malicious skill candidates via multi-view semantic expansion and uses task-based black-box competition feedback to iteratively optimize metadata for better end-to-end attack effectiveness.
result: Across four datasets and two agents, MetaCascade achieves state-of-the-art attack performance, exceeding strongest baselines by 35.53 percentage points in average attack success rate and 34.65 points under four defense settings.
conclusion: The work exposes a process-wide metadata poisoning attack surface in agent skill ecosystems, highlighting the need for defenses in skill retrieval and selection.

title: Mse Minimization For Movable Antenna Enhanced Wireless Sensing Via Array Geometry Optimization
authors: Wenrong Chen, Lipeng Zhu, Wenyan Ma, Zhi Chen, Rui Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2610.14882v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper develops adaptive movable-antenna (MA) array structures to enhance wireless sensing performance under arbitrary SNR conditions, using the AoA estimation MSE as the sensing metric. Due to the presence of strong sidelobes in the ambiguity function of sparse MA arrays, the classical CRB of AoA estimation MSE fails to characterize the true MSE in the low and medium SNR regimes, rendering CRB-optimized antenna position vector designs suboptimal for MA-enabled sensing. We derive a deterministic MSE approximation that captures the local estimation error within the mainlobe of the ambiguity function and the outlier error induced by sidelobes, providing a tractable and accurate optimization objective. We then propose three adaptive MA structures that are tailored to different hardware and computational requirements. For systems with fully independent motors, a movable free array is optimized by a two-stage greedy algorithm, which approaches the performance of the globally optimal exhaustive search but with lower computational complexity. Halving the required motors, a movable nested array fixes the dense inner subarray and adjusts only the outer-subarray spacing, reducing the optimization to a one-dimensional search. As the most hardware-efficient design, a movable twin array is proposed to adjust the inter-subarray spacing only with a single motor, while still achieving significant MSE reduction over fixed array geometries. Numerical results show that the derived approximation closely matches the true MSE compared with existing performance bounds, and that the proposed structures outperform the CRB-optimized designs by orders of magnitude in MSE across the tested low-to-medium SNR range. Moreover, it reveals that in the low-SNR regime, APV reconfiguration is more effective for improving estimation accuracy than simply increasing the number of fixed antennas.
tldr: This paper develops adaptive movable-antenna array geometries to minimize AoA estimation MSE for wireless sensing under arbitrary SNR conditions.
motivation: Classical CRB fails to characterize true MSE in sparse movable-antenna arrays due to strong sidelobes, making CRB-optimized designs suboptimal in low and medium SNR regimes.
method: The authors derive a deterministic MSE approximation capturing mainlobe local estimation error and sidelobe-induced outlier error, then propose three adaptive MA structures optimized via greedy, one-dimensional, and single-motor search algorithms.
result: The approximation closely matches true MSE, and the proposed structures outperform CRB-optimized designs by orders of magnitude in MSE; in low SNR, antenna position vector reconfiguration is more effective than adding fixed antennas.
conclusion: Adaptive movable-antenna array geometries can significantly improve wireless sensing accuracy, with hardware-efficient designs achieving substantial MSE reduction over fixed arrays.

title: Directional And Quasi-Omnidirectional Indoor Channel Measurements At Upper 6 GHz
authors: Chengsong Fu, Hongbo Zhao, Jianer Zhou, Xiongbin Yu, Weichao Li, Chen Zhuang, Meng Li, Wenquan Feng, Xiaofeng Tao
abstract: ArXiv:2610.14890v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Physical directional and quasi-omnidirectional antenna pairs are compared at 6.425--7.125 GHz over 32 position-matched indoor links per configuration: 23 line-of-sight (LOS) and nine non-LOS (NLOS) links in an open hall and an L-shaped corridor. Peak-gain normalization retains antenna-pattern weighting in the measured path loss, shadow-fading residuals, RMS delay spread (DS), and PDP-equivalent [MATH] factor. Hall LOS close-in exponents are nearly identical at 2.10/2.11 for directional\slash quasi-omnidirectional pairs, yet median DS values differ markedly at 1.78/36.52 ns. Directional DS is lower at all LOS positions, with smaller fitted shadow-fading residuals and higher [MATH] factors. Representative PDPs associate these differences with reduced off-axis delayed energy. In corridor NLOS, the directional floating-intercept slope is negative, consistent with distance-dependent antenna-pattern weighting under the fixed pointing rule, whereas the quasi-omnidirectional slope is positive and DS ordering varies by position. These results quantify practical antenna-filtered channels without angular-scan synthesis, with unequal weak-path sensitivity contributing to the observed differences.
tldr: Compares directional and quasi-omnidirectional antenna pairs for indoor channels at 6.425–7.125 GHz across LOS and NLOS links.
motivation: To quantify practical antenna-filtered channel characteristics in the upper 6 GHz band without angular-scan synthesis.
method: Measurements over 32 position-matched indoor links, analyzing path loss, shadow-fading residuals, RMS delay spread, and PDP-equivalent factor.
result: Directional antennas show lower delay spread and higher factor in hall LOS; corridor NLOS shows opposite slope trends and position-dependent delay-spread ordering.
conclusion: Antenna pattern weighting and unequal weak-path sensitivity explain the observed differences, informing indoor channel modeling for upper 6 GHz.

title: Effective DoF Collapse In Sparse Near-Field Beamforming: A Block-Rank-1 Mechanism
authors: Changhao He, Xiaojuan Zhang, Francois Chin Po Shin
abstract: ArXiv:2610.15184v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Sparse near-field arrays phase-cohere [MATH] widely separated sub-arrays of [MATH] elements and underpin distributed MIMO, satellite formations, and integrated sensing and communication. We show that their interference suppression over a protected region is set by coherence within a single sub-array rather than by the span of the formation: the effective rank of the region covariance can collapse from [MATH] to [MATH]. Two independent arguments establish this. For canonical line and disk regions each diagonal covariance block is exactly a classical concentration operator, which supplies sharp per-block rank thresholds and makes fewer than one spatial degree of freedom per sub-array a conservative design rule; an orthogonal decomposition with eigenvalue interlacing gives a nonasymptotic sufficient condition that assumes nothing about the coupling between platforms. The consequences are covariance-side and beamformer-independent: the unloaded Capon functional upper-bounds worst-case signal-to-interference ratio, while its regularized counterpart scales very differently for angularly separated and for in-cone targets. An eight-satellite LEO study validates the theory, including realized worst-case SIR.
tldr: Sparse near-field beamforming interference suppression is governed by intra-subarray coherence, causing the effective rank of the region covariance to collapse to a block-rank-1 structure.
motivation: Sparse near-field arrays are important for distributed MIMO, satellite formations, and integrated sensing and communication, but the fundamental limits of their interference suppression are not well understood.
method: The authors analyze the region covariance using two independent arguments: exact concentration-operator representations for canonical line and disk regions, and an orthogonal decomposition with eigenvalue interlacing. They validate the theory with an eight-satellite LEO study.
result: The effective rank of the covariance collapses from the full array size to a per-subarray rank, yielding sharp per-block rank thresholds. The unloaded Capon functional upper-bounds worst-case signal-to-interference ratio, with different scaling for angularly separated and in-cone targets.
conclusion: Interference suppression in sparse near-field arrays is set by coherence within a single sub-array rather than the span of the formation, providing beamformer-independent design rules and validating the block-rank-1 mechanism.

title: Cost-Aware Iteration Allocation For Sequential Multi-Fidelity First-Order Optimization
authors: Amir Ardestani-Jaafari, Warren Hare, Zhongda Huang
abstract: ArXiv:2610.14295v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Optimization can be expensive when evaluating the objective and its gradient requires a large dataset or a costly simulation. A cheaper approximation (i.e., a surrogate) can provide a useful initial point, but the work spent on that surrogate must be justified by the saving on the original problem. We study how many iterations to perform on each surrogate before switching to a more accurate objective. For a given sequence of smooth, strongly convex objectives, we use convergence bounds and distances between minimizers to construct a model of the total iteration cost. We derive closed-form two-level budgets for Nesterov's accelerated gradient method and a convex reformulation for multiple levels. We also develop an online switching rule that updates the cost comparison using the gradient at the current point. We test the techniques on a logistic-regression problem using HIGGS data. The online rule reduces weighted iteration cost in all 27 tested configurations, with a median cost of 52.8% of direct optimization. The results illustrate why updating the switching decision can be more effective than fixing the budget from an initial convergence bound.
tldr: The paper develops cost-aware iteration allocation strategies for multi-fidelity first-order convex optimization, deriving closed-form budgets and an online switching rule for Nesterov's accelerated gradient method.
motivation: Optimization with expensive objective and gradient evaluations (large datasets or costly simulations) can benefit from cheap surrogate approximations, but determining how much effort to spend on each surrogate level requires a principled cost model.
method: Using convergence bounds and distances between minimizers of a sequence of smooth strongly convex objectives, the authors construct a total iteration cost model, derive closed-form two-level budgets and a convex reformulation for multiple levels, and propose an online switching rule based on the current gradient.
result: On a logistic-regression HIGGS dataset benchmark, the online switching rule reduced weighted iteration cost in all 27 tested configurations, achieving a median cost of 52.8% relative to direct optimization.
conclusion: Adaptively updating the fidelity-switching decision online outperforms fixing the budget from an initial convergence bound, illustrating the value of cost-aware dynamic allocation in multi-fidelity optimization.

title: Fixed Points For Uniformly Asymptotically H\"older-Lipschitz Mappings
authors: Carlos S\'ergio R. Da Silva Luciano G. Josino
abstract: ArXiv:2610.14327v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, we show that if [MATH] is a nonempty, closed, bounded, and convex subset of [MATH] and [MATH] where [MATH] denotes the Bynum normal structure coefficient, then every uniformly asymptotically H\"older [MATH]-Lipschitz mapping [MATH] has a fixed point. To achieve this, it was necessary to guarantee the existence of a subsequence of a bounded sequence whose asymptotic diameter is controlled by the quantity [MATH] introduced by Jim\'enez-Melado, while simultaneously preserving the asymptotic radii at every point of the closure of the linear span generated by the original sequence. This allowed us to remove the H\"older exponent from the calculations and obtain a H\"older-type extension of the Casini--Maluta, Lim--Xu, and, consequently, Kim--Xu theorems.
tldr: The paper proves a fixed point theorem for uniformly asymptotically Hölder-Lipschitz mappings on closed bounded convex subsets of a Banach space, extending classical results via a new control on asymptotic diameters and radii.
motivation: Classical fixed point results (Casini–Maluta, Lim–Xu, Kim–Xu) rely on normal structure coefficients and control of asymptotic diameters; the authors seek a Hölder-type generalization that removes the Hölder exponent from the calculations.
method: Using the Bynum normal structure coefficient and a quantity introduced by Jiménez-Melado, they construct a subsequence of a bounded sequence whose asymptotic diameter is controlled while preserving asymptotic radii over the closure of the span of the original sequence.
result: Whenever a certain coefficient condition holds, every uniformly asymptotically Hölder-Lipschitz mapping on a nonempty closed bounded convex subset admits a fixed point, yielding Hölder-type extensions of the Casini–Maluta and Lim–Xu theorems.
conclusion: The work provides a new geometric fixed point criterion in Banach spaces, but it lies entirely within nonlinear functional analysis with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Signed Quantities And Quadrilaterals: Geometry Without Cases
authors: George-Rubin Thomas
abstract: ArXiv:2610.14452v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Ordinary angles and unsigned areas discard orientation, and much of the case analysis in plane geometry is the price of that loss. Signed quantities (directed angles, oriented areas and directed distances) keep the signs and so let one argument serve for every configuration. We illustrate this with results that hold uniformly for convex, concave and crossed quadrilaterals: the diagonal area formula, an identity expressing one diagonal in terms of the sides and the other diagonal, a test for a pair of parallel sides, a theorem on equidiagonal quadrilaterals (such a quadrilateral has a pair of equal opposite sides if and only if it has a pair of parallel opposite sides), and a single ratio of directed distances that decides whether the vertices lie on an ellipse, only on hyperbolas, or on a circle.
tldr: A classical plane-geometry paper showing that using signed quantities (directed angles, oriented areas, directed distances) yields uniform, case-free proofs for quadrilaterals ranging from convex to crossed.
motivation: Ordinary unsigned angles and areas discard orientation, forcing tedious case-by-case analyses in elementary plane geometry; the author aims to eliminate this case analysis by retaining signs.
method: Systematic use of signed geometric quantities — directed angles, oriented areas, and directed distances — to derive identities that hold uniformly across all quadrilateral configurations.
result: Uniform results include the diagonal area formula, an identity relating one diagonal to the sides and the other diagonal, a parallel-sides test, a theorem on equidiagonal quadrilaterals, and a single directed-distance ratio deciding whether vertices lie on an ellipse, hyperbola, or circle.
conclusion: Signed quantities provide a cleaner, more general framework for plane geometry, replacing configuration-dependent casework with a single unified argument.

title: Sum Rate Maximization For Practical RIS-Enhanced Rate-Splitting Multiple Access Systems
authors: Qian Zhang, Xuejun Cheng, Jiaming Shi, Yufei Zhao, Rugui Yao, Ye Fan
abstract: ArXiv:2610.14765v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RIS) combined with rate-splitting multiple access (RSMA) provide a promising solution for improving the spectral efficiency (SE) of sixth-generation (6G) communication systems. However, most existing studies neglect the practical coupling between the RIS phase shift and amplitude, which may cause phase-shift mismatch and significant performance loss. In this paper, we investigate the multiuser sum-rate maximization problem for practical RIS-enhanced RSMA systems considering amplitude-phase coupling. To address the resulting non-convex problem, an effective variable separation algorithm is proposed. The proposed algorithm is compatible with RIS reflecting optimization under the continuous phase shift or any amplitude-phase coupling relationship and can also be directly extended to practical RIS-enhanced NOMA and OMA systems. Simulation results demonstrate performance gain of over 190\% compared with the ideal-RIS-based benchmark, while the proposed RSMA scheme significantly outperforms the corresponding NOMA and OMA schemes.
tldr: This paper studies sum-rate maximization for RIS-enhanced rate-splitting multiple access systems while accounting for practical amplitude-phase coupling at the RIS.
motivation: Existing RIS-aided communication designs often ignore the coupling between RIS phase shift and amplitude, leading to performance loss from phase-shift mismatch.
method: The authors formulate a non-convex multiuser sum-rate maximization problem and propose a variable separation algorithm compatible with continuous phase shifts or arbitrary amplitude-phase coupling relationships.
result: Simulations show over 190% performance gain compared with an ideal-RIS benchmark, and the proposed RSMA scheme outperforms corresponding NOMA and OMA schemes.
conclusion: The proposed algorithm improves spectral efficiency in practical RIS-enhanced RSMA systems and can be extended to RIS-enhanced NOMA and OMA systems.

title: Best-of-Both-Worlds Fair Division Via Subsidies
authors: Rohit Vaish Surya Panchapakesan
abstract: ArXiv:2610.14994v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the relationship between fair division with [MATH] and [MATH] (BoBW) fairness for indivisible items. We prove a general reduction of BoBW existence to envy-freeability. Specifically, for any scale-free ex-post property [MATH] (e.g., EF1, EFX, PO) and any scale-free valuation class [MATH] (e.g, additive, submodular, subadditive, monotone), if every instance in [MATH] admits a [MATH]-allocation that can be made envy-free using subsidies, then every such instance admits an ex-ante envy-free lottery supported on [MATH]-allocations. The proof uses linear programming duality. As applications, the reduction gives alternative proofs of BoBW existence results for additive goods, chores, and mixtures of goods and chores. The converse of our general reduction holds for two agents but fails for three: We provide a four-good counterexample with monotone submodular valuations where an ex-ante envy-free and ex-post EF1 lottery exists, but no allocation is simultaneously EF1 and envy-freeable. For lexicographic valuations, we prove simultaneous EFX, Pareto optimality, and envy-freeability (and hence BoBW guarantees for EFX+PO) for three agents, and show that even EFX and envy-freeability can be incompatible for four agents.
tldr: The paper establishes a general reduction showing that best-of-both-worlds (ex-ante envy-free, ex-post fair) lotteries for indivisible items exist whenever allocations can be made envy-free via subsidies, using LP duality.
motivation: BoBW fairness for indivisible goods and chores is important in fair division, but existence results have been established piecemeal for specific properties and valuation classes; a unifying principle was lacking.
method: The authors prove a general reduction from BoBW existence to envy-freeability for any scale-free ex-post property and scale-free valuation class, via linear programming duality, and study a converse for small numbers of agents.
result: The reduction reproves BoBW results for additive goods, chores, and mixtures; the converse holds for two agents but fails for three (a four-good monotone submodular counterexample), and for lexicographic valuations EFX+PO+envy-freeability holds for three agents but EFX and envy-freeability can conflict for four.
conclusion: The work provides a clean duality-based framework linking subsidies and BoBW fairness, while delineating sharp limits of the equivalence for more than two agents.

title: Siren: A Nonlinear Rankine-source Boundary Element Solver For The Stationary Motion Of A Marine Vehicle In Calm Water
authors: Daniele Peri
abstract: ArXiv:2610.14027v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: SIREN (Ship Inviscid Resistance and Elevation eNgine) is a Rankine-source panel solver for the steady wave resistance of a ship, in the tradition of Dawson's method. The free-surface condition is linearised about a base flow, and the linearisation is iterated. In the present formulation the base flow is the solution of a Neumann problem on the actual boundary: sources on the entire hull, wet and dry, and on the free surface panels, with impermeability imposed on both, so that the free surface acts as a rigid lid at the position it currently occupies. This replaces the classical double-body flow, whose image about z=0 is meaningful only for a flat surface and a hull cut at z=0, and it removes the need for desingularised free-surface panels. In the non-linear iteration the free-surface panels are moved rigidly in the vertical to the relaxed wave elevation at their centroid, the hull panels are marked wet or dry against the moved surface, and the base flow is recomputed on the moved geometry; impermeability applies to the whole hull regardless of this marking, which is used only to select which panels enter the force integral, and under-relaxation is confined to the passes where the non-linear correction accumulates without being reset. The radiation condition is imposed by a one-row upstream shift of the collocation points, and the wave resistance is obtained by pressure integration and, independently, by transverse wave-cut analysis.
tldr: SIREN is a nonlinear Rankine-source boundary element solver for steady wave resistance of a ship in calm water, iterating a linearized free-surface condition with a Neumann base flow.
motivation: The paper aims to improve ship wave resistance prediction by replacing the classical double-body flow linearization with a Neumann problem on the actual hull and free surface.
method: A Rankine-source panel method is used with impermeability on wet and dry hull panels and free-surface panels; the free surface is iteratively updated as a rigid lid, and the radiation condition is imposed by an upstream shift of collocation points.
result: The wave resistance is computed by pressure integration and independently by transverse wave-cut analysis, with under-relaxation controlling the nonlinear iteration.
conclusion: The formulation removes the need for desingularized free-surface panels and offers an alternative iterative approach to steady ship wave resistance problems.

title: Global Regularization Of The Spatial Elliptic Restricted Three-body Problem: Quaternionic, Hamiltonian Formulation
authors: Kenshiro Oguri
abstract: ArXiv:2610.13969v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Any objects in space may encounter singularity due to the inverse-square law of the gravitational force, hindering the analysis and propagation of particle motion in space. Regularization in celestial mechanics removes such gravitational singularities in equations of motion by transforming the time and coordinates. This paper addresses a class of regularization methods known as global regularization for restricted three-body problems (R3BPs), which simultaneously removes the two singularities (e.g., Earth and Moon in cislunar space). It enables analysis, propagation, and prediction of particle motion throughout the domain of R3BPs, which is in stark contrast to regularizing each singularity individually. In particular, this paper develops a formulation for global regularization of the spatial elliptic R3BP (ER3BP) under external perturbations. The presented formulation leverages mathematical tools from quaternionic (hyper-complex) algebra and Hamiltonian mechanics. This approach enables us to (i) elegantly handle the four-dimensional coordinates arising from the dimension-lifting operation for spatial regularization, (ii) systematically derive the coordinate-momentum transformation while preserving the canonical structure and incorporating perturbing forces, and (iii) provide geometric insights for analyzing the regularity of the transformation, resulting Hamiltonian, and dynamical flow. Numerical examples demonstrate the validity of the mathematical results as well as significant numerical benefits of the regularization formulation in perturbed Earth-Moon ER3BP.
tldr: This paper develops a quaternionic Hamiltonian formulation for global regularization of the spatial elliptic restricted three-body problem under external perturbations.
motivation: Gravitational singularities from the inverse-square law hinder accurate propagation and analysis of particle motion in restricted three-body problems, especially when both primaries create singularities.
method: The authors use quaternionic algebra and Hamiltonian mechanics to derive coordinate-momentum transformations that remove both singularities simultaneously while preserving canonical structure and including perturbations.
result: The formulation provides geometric insights into regularity of the transformation and dynamics, and numerical examples in the perturbed Earth-Moon elliptic restricted three-body problem demonstrate its validity and numerical benefits.
conclusion: The proposed global regularization method enables more robust analysis and propagation of trajectories throughout the spatial elliptic restricted three-body problem domain, particularly with perturbations.

title: How Long Is A Game Of Uno? A Counting Law For Large Hands And The Wild Draw Four Hoard
authors: Pragyaan Gaur
abstract: ArXiv:2610.14076v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the length of one round of Uno under the official rules, for N players who each start with M cards. The fastest possible round takes at least M turns with two players and at least 2M-1 turns with three or more, and both bounds are attained for small M. An exact search over random deals shows that real deals rarely allow them. Under the official rules a round has no maximum length. Under forced play the probability that a round lasts more than t turns decays exponentially in t at a rate that does not depend on M. Our main result concerns very large hands. If every card a player ever holds is eventually played, a round lasts (27/19)NM turns to first order, and the constant depends only on the composition of the deck. The official rule that a Wild Draw Four may only be played by a player who holds no card of the current colour breaks this law. Every large hand hoards Wild Draw Fours, M/23 of them per player, and the round ends with a dumping endgame. For an even number of players this gives (53/46)NM turns. For an odd number of players the dumping cannot alternate round the table, and the endgame settles into a seating pattern whose turn rate we compute numerically. Simulations with up to 32,000 cards per hand support these limits. Finally we solve a small strategy game: with two players the Nash equilibrium over a family of 48 strategies is a single pure strategy that wins 62.8% of rounds against uniformly random play.
tldr: The paper derives counting laws and asymptotic limits for the length of Uno rounds under official and forced play, including Wild Draw Four hoarding effects and a small strategy-game Nash equilibrium.
motivation: The authors aim to mathematically characterize the duration of a round of Uno, a popular card game, under various rule sets and player numbers.
method: Combinatorial counting, exact search over random deals, probabilistic analysis of forced play, asymptotic scaling arguments for large hands, and numerical simulation with up to 32,000 cards per hand; also Nash equilibrium computation for 48 strategies with two players.
result: Forced-play round length decays exponentially; for large hands with all cards eventually played, the length scales as (27/19)NM turns, with Wild Draw Four hoarding leading to (53/46)NM for even players and a more complex pattern for odd players.
conclusion: Uno round lengths follow precise scaling laws that depend on deck composition and player count, and a single pure strategy is Nash equilibrium against uniformly random play in a restricted two-player game.

title: Philip L. Roe, The British Scientist. The Cranfield Years And Beyond
authors: Eleuterio F. Toro
abstract: ArXiv:2610.14087v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Philip L. Roe, the renowned British scientist, passed away on April 26, 2026, at the age of 87, while Professor Emeritus at the University of Michigan. My association with Phil Roe began in 1984, when he joined the Cranfield Institute of Technology, UK, as Professor of Computational Fluid Dynamics, while I was a postdoctoral research fellow at the same institution. For more than four decades, his incisive ideas, physical principles and distinctive approach to research on numerical methods for solving hyperbolic partial differential equations have had a lasting influence on my own approach to research in the field. Here I recount some personal memories and anecdotes emerging from the rewarding experience of interacting with Phil during the Cranfield years and beyond. I also review, quite succinctly in places, some of the main research topics that he pursued throughout much of his academic career. These notes are intended as a modest homage to Roe's impact on the subject, as well as to his influence on the careers of generations of scientists in both academia and industry.
tldr: A personal and scientific homage to Philip L. Roe, recounting his career in computational fluid dynamics and numerical methods for hyperbolic PDEs.
motivation: The author aims to commemorate Roe's influence on the field of computational fluid dynamics and on generations of scientists following his death in 2026.
method: Narrative memoir combining personal anecdotes from the Cranfield years and beyond with a succinct review of Roe's main research topics.
result: A historical and biographical account of Roe's contributions, notably numerical schemes (e.g., Roe solver) for hyperbolic conservation laws.
conclusion: The notes serve as a modest tribute to Roe's lasting impact on numerical methods and on the careers of researchers in academia and industry.

title: Global Convergence And Reliable Stopping In A Safeguarded Modified Anderson--Bj\"orck Method
authors: Nedelcho Ganchovski Latchezar Tomov
abstract: ArXiv:2610.14193v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The modified Anderson-Bjorck (modAB) method was first proposed in 2023 by Ganchovski and Traykov for solving nonlinear equations in structural mechanics. It was improved further in 2026 by introducing better switching criteria with account to function symmetry, and bisection fallback based on measuring the bracket reduction rate. Although the algorithm demonstrated superior performance across a great variety of functions, it lacked formal mathematical analysis and proof of convergence. In addition, some discrepancies were noted by L. Tomov in the latest version that need to be addressed: premature application of the Anderson-Bjorck (AB) correction on the first AB step, caused by retaining the endpoint-update record from the preceding bisection step, and using the corrected endpoint ordinates in symmetry factor calculation instead of the true residuals. The purpose of the present paper is to provide rigorous mathematical proof of global convergence in exact arithmetic, remove the above discrepancies, and provide floating-point safeguards for interpolation, switching and stopping, with explicit treatment of infinite and NaN values, underflow, overflow and round-off errors. These safeguards do not certify the accuracy of the supplied function values. Additional performance improvement was introduced by allowing for early bisection fallback when AB fails to make progress on reducing either the bracket width or the residual, while retaining a finite bound on consecutive exceptions to the prescribed width condition.
tldr: The paper provides a rigorous proof of global convergence and floating-point safeguards for a safeguarded modified Anderson-Bjorck method for solving nonlinear equations.
motivation: The modified Anderson-Bjorck method showed strong practical performance but lacked formal convergence analysis and contained implementation discrepancies related to switching and endpoint updates.
method: The authors prove global convergence in exact arithmetic, correct the premature Anderson-Bjorck correction and symmetry-factor calculation, and add floating-point safeguards for interpolation, switching, and stopping under overflow, underflow, NaN, and round-off errors.
result: The corrected method retains global convergence and gains improved reliability and performance through early bisection fallback when progress is insufficient, while bounding consecutive exceptions to the width condition.
conclusion: The work strengthens the theoretical foundation of the modified Anderson-Bjorck method and provides a more robust numerical implementation for nonlinear equation solving.

title: Euler Cutting Planes For Fractional CVaR Programming
authors: Pranay Seshadri, Hubert Dzieciol, Zhe Feng, Alan Tua
abstract: ArXiv:2610.14656v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We maximise expected reward per unit of marginal tail risk, a reward-to-CVaR ratio against a baseline. The standard Dinkelbach route re-solves a Rockafellar--Uryasev LP or QP with one auxiliary variable per tail scenario at each multiplier update. Our method eliminates the multiplier iteration and keeps scenario auxiliaries out of the master, while still evaluating tail risk to generate cuts. A Charnes--Cooper/Schaible homogenisation removes the reward/risk multiplier, and the remaining convex constraint is separated on demand: each cut coefficient is an Euler allocation vector, read off a ranking and an average. The result is a single convex program, finitely terminating at the global optimum, with size independent of S --- an LP in [MATH] variables, or a second-order cone program in [MATH] for a concave quadratic numerator. The method runs 20--100 times faster than the exact Dinkelbach formulation and only needs single-digit cut counts.
tldr: The paper introduces Euler cutting planes for fractional CVaR programming, eliminating multiplier iteration and reducing problem size for reward-to-tail-risk optimization.
motivation: Standard Dinkelbach methods for maximizing reward-to-CVaR ratios repeatedly solve LPs or QPs with auxiliary variables, which is computationally expensive.
method: The authors use Charnes-Cooper/Schaible homogenization to remove the reward/risk multiplier and separate a convex constraint on demand, with cut coefficients derived from Euler allocation vectors.
result: The resulting single convex program terminates finitely at the global optimum, scales independently of the number of tail scenarios, and runs 20-100 times faster than exact Dinkelbach with only single-digit cut counts.
conclusion: Euler cutting planes offer an efficient exact alternative for fractional CVaR optimization, avoiding multiplier iterations and scenario auxiliary variables.

title: TrustPaper For Forged Pdf With Issuer Fingerprints
authors: Yassine El Jakani, Mohamed Nadir Rhazi, Othmane Meknassi, Oualid Chbiki, Mounira Msahli, Francois Gonnet
abstract: ArXiv:2610.14132v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Sick leave certificates are increasingly delivered as PDF files by online teleconsultation platforms, and can be altered in minutes with free editors. Generic PDF scanners report how a file was built, but cannot tell whether that construction is legitimate: an incremental update, an embedded font or a given producer string is normal for one issuer and anomalous for another. We present TrustPaper solution, an issuer aware forensic approach that combines three elements: the claimed issuer of the document, a reference fingerprint learned beforehand from genuine documents of that issuer, and an explainable combination of evidence from several forensic modules. Fingerprints are stored as versioned declarative profiles, and every anomaly keeps its observed value, expected value and triggering rule. We formalize the threat model, the fingerprint and the scoring model, and evaluate the open-source prototype on a controlled corpus documents from two issuers and six forgery techniques. With the issuer fingerprint, all forgeries made by opportunistic and metadata-aware attackers are flagged with no false positive on genuine test documents.
tldr: TrustPaper is an issuer-aware forensic framework that detects forged PDF sick-leave certificates by comparing documents against per-issuer fingerprints learned from genuine files.
motivation: Online teleconsultation platforms increasingly issue PDF certificates that are trivially editable, and generic PDF scanners cannot distinguish legitimate construction artifacts from forged ones because anomaly patterns are issuer-dependent.
method: The approach combines the claimed issuer identity, a versioned declarative reference fingerprint learned from genuine documents of that issuer, and an explainable fusion of evidence from multiple forensic modules, formalized via a threat model and scoring model.
result: On a controlled corpus spanning two issuers and six forgery techniques, the open-source prototype flagged all forgeries from opportunistic and metadata-aware attackers with zero false positives on genuine test documents.
conclusion: Issuer-specific fingerprinting with explainable evidence combination offers an effective and low-false-positive defense against document forgery in digital certificate workflows.

title: ByteMark: A Unified Byte-Level Watermark For Detection Across Language Models
authors: Runze Li Xiaopu Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2610.14427v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As watermarking of LLM-generated text enters deployment, users increasingly need to check text whose source is unknown. Existing detectors read the watermark through a specific tokenizer or embedding pipeline, and even if all providers adopted the same watermarking method, differences in these representations would leave their watermarks incompatible, and the text alone does not reveal which representation produced it. We propose ByteMark, a unified watermarking scheme that defines its signal on the UTF-8 bytes of published text. Models with different tokenizers embed this signal under one public specification and key, and a single detector verifies the text from the text and key alone. When the tokenizer or embedding model of a baseline detector is replaced, its detection degrades sharply, whereas ByteMark, which uses neither, retains its detection rate; ByteMark also remains detectable when participating models continue or rewrite the text.
tldr: ByteMark proposes a byte-level watermarking scheme for LLM-generated text that remains detectable across different tokenizers and embedding models.
motivation: Existing LLM watermark detectors rely on specific tokenizers or embedding pipelines, making watermarks incompatible across models and preventing source-agnostic verification.
method: The scheme defines the watermark signal on UTF-8 bytes of published text, allowing models with different tokenizers to embed the same signal under a public specification and key, and a single detector to verify text using only the text and key.
result: ByteMark retains high detection rates when baseline detectors degrade due to tokenizer or embedding model replacement, and it remains detectable even when models continue or rewrite the text.
conclusion: ByteMark provides a unified, representation-independent watermark for LLM text provenance, enabling reliable detection without access to the original tokenizer or embedding pipeline.

title: SecReason: Vulnerability Detection And In-Stream Self-Repair For Llm Code Generation
authors: Ruidong Han, Zhensu Sun, Chengyan Ma, Yuqing Niu, Siqi Ma, David Lo
abstract: ArXiv:2610.14453v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) may introduce security vulnerabilities into generated code, which can persist into production when verification focuses on functional correctness. Existing defenses act before, during, or after generation, but none inspects the code during generation. Security prompts and retrieved security knowledge act before any code exists, constrained decoding limits token choices but cannot guide repair, and post-hoc repair must regenerate the full response. Reasoning LLMs draft code early in their streamed chain of thought, and in this pre-delivery window the code exists only inside the reasoning stream. We present SecReason, an in-stream defense that monitors this window. Dual-track incremental scanning applies security rules, checking each statement as it is emitted and tracing dataflows across the accumulated code. When a security rule fires, SecReason interrupts generation, inserts an in-stream warning, and resumes decoding, so the model repairs the draft within the same reasoning trace without regenerating the full response. On tasks where unassisted generation introduces vulnerabilities, \system raises the share of runs delivering secure and functionally correct code from below 15\% to 72.8\%--98.1\% on and . \system consumes fewer tokens than post-hoc repair, and when security rules misfire on secure code, it limits the functional regressions from false warnings.
tldr: SecReason is an in-stream defense that monitors LLM reasoning traces during code generation to detect and repair security vulnerabilities before the code is finalized.
motivation: LLMs often generate insecure code, and existing defenses either act before code exists, constrain token-level decoding, or require costly post-hoc regeneration.
method: SecReason performs dual-track incremental scanning and dataflow tracing over streamed reasoning, interrupts generation when security rules fire, inserts an in-stream warning, and lets the model repair the draft within the same trace.
result: On vulnerable-generation tasks, SecReason raises secure-and-functional code delivery from below 15% to 72.8%–98.1%, while consuming fewer tokens than post-hoc repair and limiting functional regressions from false warnings.
conclusion: In-stream vulnerability detection and self-repair during LLM reasoning can substantially improve code security without full regeneration.

title: Diffusion-Based Auctions For Multi-Winner Banner Ads
authors: Lilian Sun, Henry Huang, Fucheng Warren Zhu, Giannis Daras, Constantinos Daskalakis
abstract: ArXiv:2610.14473v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a new framework for banner ad auctions, leveraging diffusion models to allow for multiple bidders to co-win a single banner ad opportunity, and in particular influence the ad shown on the banner depending on the strength of their bids, enabling a far richer outcome space compared to standard banner ad auctions, where there is a single winner who shows their ad. In our framework, the outcomes are images (what ad to show) and each bidder expresses their preferences over outcomes by declaring their value per unit of alignment between the image chosen by the mechanism and a textual description of their desired image. Our proposed mechanism combines the advertisers' bids and textual descriptions into a score that drives the reverse process of a diffusion model. This is used to sample a set of candidate images from which the welfare maximizing one is eventually chosen. Extensive experimentation evaluates our proposed mechanism around the following axes: (1) efficiency improvements of our allocation rule relative to the single-winner allocation rule; (2) monotonicity of our allocation rule; and (3) approximate incentive compatibility when combining our allocation rule with Myerson lemma-based or Clarke rule-based payments. Improvements along all these axes are shown with the number of Monte Carlo samples. Meanwhile, these benefits are attained while preserving the image quality.
tldr: The paper proposes an auction mechanism that uses diffusion models to let multiple bidders jointly influence the banner ad image shown, sampling candidate images and selecting the welfare-maximizing one.
motivation: Standard banner ad auctions select a single winning advertiser, which limits the outcome space; the authors aim to enable richer multi-winner outcomes by letting bidders' preferences shape the generated ad image.
method: Bidders declare values per unit of alignment between a diffusion-generated image and their textual descriptions; these bids and texts are combined into a score that steers the reverse diffusion process, from which candidate images are sampled and the welfare-maximizing one chosen, with Myerson- or Clarke-style payments.
result: Experiments show improved allocation efficiency over single-winner rules, monotonicity of the allocation, and approximate incentive compatibility, with gains increasing in the number of Monte Carlo samples while preserving image quality.
conclusion: Diffusion-based multi-winner auctions can expand the allocation outcome space and improve welfare in ad auctions, though the work is entirely in mechanism design and generative modelling with no connection to quantum information.

title: Decision Uncertainty-Oriented Watermarking (duow): Securing Multi-Agent Routing Against Policy Cloning
authors: Ziming Zhang, Li Li, Guorui Feng, Hanzhou Wu, Xinpeng Zhang, Athanasios V. Vasilakos
abstract: ArXiv:2610.14606v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Routing policies in Multi-Agent Systems (MAS) represent valuable intellectual property, yet their exposure through execution logs creates significant risks of unauthorized policy cloning. Existing agent watermarking methods protect intellectual property by modifying internal generation processes, such as perturbing token sampling distributions or injecting structural mutations into action trajectories, which may compromise task fidelity or suffer from limited transferability across heterogeneous platforms. To address these limitations, we propose Decision Uncertainty-Oriented Watermarking (DUOW), a lightweight framework that operates at the external decision layer without modifying model parameters or generated outputs. DUOW introduces a plug-and-play scoring mechanism that evaluates candidate agents from semantic and operational perspectives, identifies functionally redundant routing decisions, and selectively redirects choices among equivalent alternatives to embed ownership signals. By coupling watermark behaviors with utility-preserving routing decisions, DUOW enables cloned policies to retain ownership signals during policy imitation while increasing the difficulty of watermark removal. A confidence-driven adaptive threshold dynamically determines embedding opportunities, balancing watermark capacity and task fidelity under diverse routing contexts. Extensive evaluations on four multi-agent routing benchmarks demonstrate that DUOW preserves high task utility, achieves reliable ownership verification under up to 90% log erasure, and introduces negligible computational overhead, with an average per-step latency of 0.043 ms and total embedding overhead below 0.54 ms.
tldr: DUOW is a lightweight watermarking framework for multi-agent routing policies that embeds ownership signals by redirecting functionally redundant decisions without modifying model parameters or outputs.
motivation: Routing policies in multi-agent systems are valuable intellectual property but are vulnerable to cloning from execution logs, and existing watermarking methods can harm task fidelity or generalize poorly.
method: DUOW operates at the external decision layer, using a plug-and-play scoring mechanism to identify equivalent routing alternatives and a confidence-driven adaptive threshold to selectively redirect choices, embedding watermarks while preserving utility.
result: Across four multi-agent routing benchmarks, DUOW maintains high task utility, enables reliable ownership verification even under 90% log erasure, and adds negligible overhead (0.043 ms average per-step latency, <0.54 ms total embedding).
conclusion: DUOW provides an effective and efficient approach to protecting multi-agent routing policies from unauthorized cloning without altering model internals or degrading performance.

title: Towards Merging-conditional Backdoor Unalignment Against Large Language Models
authors: Yukun Chen, Yidou Chen, Yiming Li, Xinyu Zhang, Baosong Yang, Hongwei Yao, Zhan Qin
abstract: ArXiv:2610.14701v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Model merging has become widely adopted for enhancing the task-specific performance of Large Language Models (LLMs) without additional training. While the specialized model from third-party platforms may undergo safety audits (e.g., backdoor detection), we reveal a novel and critical threat: One-sided Merging-Conditional Backdoor (OMCB). OMCB remains dormant and undetectable within one standalone model but activates upon merging, triggering safety unalignment. We first theoretically analyze the existence and geometric location of OMCB, revealing that the parameter shift crossing safety decision boundaries is the main cause of backdoor activation. Building upon this insight, we propose SMOKE, a meta-learning-based attack framework. SMOKE implants OMCB via a bi-level optimization strategy: the inner loop synthesizes surrogate meta-vectors through random low-rank initialization and finite-step maximization, while the outer loop optimizes the target model by simulating the merging process. Furthermore, preliminary analysis shows that the injected OMCB has bounded generalization loss under unknown merging configurations. Extensive experiments across diverse model architectures and merging techniques validate the effectiveness of SMOKE and its resistance to existing backdoor detections, highlighting a significant yet previously overlooked vulnerability in the model merging paradigm.
tldr: The paper reveals a one-sided merging-conditional backdoor (OMCB) in large language models and proposes SMOKE, a meta-learning attack that remains dormant in standalone models but triggers safety unalignment upon model merging.
motivation: Model merging is widely used to combine specialized LLMs, and while individual models may pass safety audits, there is a novel threat that a backdoor can activate only after merging, bypassing existing detection.
method: The authors theoretically analyze the existence and geometric location of OMCB, identifying parameter shift across safety decision boundaries as the activation cause. They propose SMOKE, a bi-level optimization meta-learning framework that implants OMCB by synthesizing surrogate meta-vectors and optimizing the target model through simulated merging.
result: Extensive experiments across diverse architectures and merging techniques show SMOKE effectively injects the backdoor, resists existing backdoor detections, and maintains bounded generalization loss under unknown merging configurations.
conclusion: The work exposes a previously overlooked vulnerability in the model merging paradigm, demonstrating that safety checks on individual models are insufficient, and calls for new defenses tailored to merging-conditional threats.

title: acousticHelmholtzFoam: An MPI-parallel Unstructured Finite-volume Solver For Frequency-domain Acoustics In Heterogeneous Two-phase Media With Perfectly Matched Layers
authors: Chuanchao Xu, Jun Liu, Dieter Bothe, Tomislav Maric
abstract: ArXiv:2610.14057v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: acousticHelmholtzFoam is an OpenFOAM application that computes time-harmonic acoustic pressure fields in heterogeneous gas-liquid media on unstructured polyhedral meshes. The complex pressure is stored as real and imaginary volume fields, the material coefficients are constructed from a volume-of-fluid phase fraction with geometric face-fraction averaging, and open boundaries are truncated by Cartesian perfectly matched layers (PMLs) whose damping tensor is generated by the companion utility setPMLFields. The two coupled real-valued equations are discretized with the cell-centred finite-volume operators of OpenFOAM and assembled explicitly, including processor couplings and boundary contributions, into a distributed PETSc matrix that is solved by default with the MUMPS sparse direct solver. The solver writes pressure amplitude, complex velocity, acoustic radiation pressure and time-averaged momentum flux for acoustic-force evaluation. This paper documents the implemented equations, the case interface, the assembly and solution algorithm, the build procedure and the test infrastructure. A layered gas-liquid-PML case with an analytical solution serves as an end-to-end regression: on 8000 cells the whole-domain relative complex-pressure error is [MATH], and serial and MPI solutions on up to eight ranks agree to within [MATH] in relative [MATH] norm. A single-axis acoustic-levitator height sweep with constant-volume spheroidal drops demonstrates the two-phase material input and the force output, and strong- and problem-size-scaling measurements characterize the direct-solver workflow. The numerical formulation and its verification are presented in a companion paper (arXiv:2610.01593).
tldr: An MPI-parallel OpenFOAM solver for frequency-domain acoustics in heterogeneous two-phase media using finite-volume discretization and perfectly matched layers.
motivation: Acoustic pressure fields in gas-liquid media require efficient numerical tools that handle complex geometries, open boundaries, and acoustic radiation forces.
method: The solver stores complex pressure as real and imaginary fields, constructs material coefficients from volume-of-fluid phase fractions, truncates open boundaries with Cartesian PMLs, and assembles a distributed PETSc matrix solved by MUMPS.
result: Regression tests show relative complex-pressure error on 8000 cells and serial/MPI agreement up to eight ranks; a levitator height sweep demonstrates two-phase input and force output.
conclusion: acousticHelmholtzFoam provides a verified, scalable framework for acoustic-force evaluation in two-phase flows, with numerical formulation presented in a companion paper.

title: Consumption Adjustment With Mean-reverting Risk Premia: A Singular Stochastic Control Approach
authors: Gugyum Ha, Junkee Jeon, Jehan Oh
